findings.why: From lf.nao_deliver onward, Umi speaks to Nao in plain form (勝手ね, 届けてくれる?, then lf.umi_after 「届けてね」, and sa.epi_lf 「あんた言ったよね」). This post-game line, addressed only to Nao, returns to full です/ます. It does follow her polite counter greeting (#9bbd6ec318), so it could be her composed office voice. Without a cue, though, it sounds like the relationship has stepped back.
findings.direction: If the step back is not intended, keep the office greeting polite and move the Nao-only line to her plain voice, e.g. 「……返事の返事が来たの。」. If it is intended, a narration cue would make the change readable.

findings.speaker: lf_masaru
findings.text: 記録館の人、少し驚いてから、「では五十個で」だって。最初からそう言えっての！
findings.en: The Records Hall fellow looked startled, then said "fifty, then". Should've said so in the first place!
findings.why: 「言えっての」 (= 言えというの, an exasperated retort) is an unusual contraction that a learner cannot parse from って or の alone. 「だって」 in the same line is the quotative だって (= と言っていた), not 'because'. The line is fine as speech.
findings.direction: Add word help: 〜っての = 〜と言っているんだ, exasperated emphasis on a command, and だって (quoting) = they said.

findings.speaker: any (comp!=suzu: Nao, Mio or Ren)
findings.addressee: pc (close travelling companion, right after the pc played the straight man)
findings.text: 意外な才能だな。
findings.en: An unexpected talent.
findings.why: The 〜だな ending fits only Nao. In the whole game Mio never ends a remark to the pc with 〜だな (her one だな is self-talk: 嫌だな), and Ren never says だな at all. Spoken by Mio or Ren, this line sounds like a different character.
findings.direction: Split by companion, or keep the line neutral for Mio and Ren; e.g. for Mio/Ren '意外な才能ですね'.

findings.speaker: any (comp!=suzu: Nao, Mio or Ren)
findings.text: 台詞を一緒に読んでみませんか。名前より先に、役が戻るかもしれない。
findings.en: Shall we read your lines together? The part might come back before the name does.
findings.why: The polite invitation 〜てみませんか suits Mio and Ren, but Nao speaks plain to everyone, strangers included. Nao's only other polite lines in the game are quoted or teaching examples. From Nao, this would sound out of character.
findings.direction: Give Nao a separate plain line and keep the polite one for Mio and Ren; e.g. for Nao '台詞、一緒に読んでみるか'.

findings.speaker: any (comp!=suzu: Nao, Mio or Ren)
findings.addressee: pc (companion), half to self, about the kuroko
findings.text: 見えているのに、いないことにするのか。……声をかけてみよう。
findings.en: You can see it, and it counts as not there? …Say something to it.
findings.why: The plain 〜のか plus volitional 〜てみよう is Nao's voice. Ren never addresses the pc with 〜てみよう, and uses 〜のか only once, in a monologue. Mio's suggestions to the pc are normally 〜ましょう (行きましょう, 進みましょう).
findings.direction: Split by companion, or soften to a form all three would use; e.g. for Ren/Mio '……声をかけてみましょう'.

findings.speaker: any (comp!=mio: Nao, Ren or Suzu)
findings.addressee: pc (companion), aside about the tonic seller
findings.text: 何でも治るは、何も治らないと同じかもね。
findings.en: "Cures everything" might be the same as "cures nothing".
findings.why: The soft かもね fits only Suzu. Nao says かもな (8 times) and never かもね. Ren says かもしれません (34 times) and never かもね. There is also a grammar problem when spoken: without quotation brackets, 何も治らないと同じ needs の (何も治らないのと同じ).
findings.direction: Split by companion, or recast so the quotation is audible and the ending fits each voice; e.g. '「何でも治る」ってのは、「何も治らない」のと同じだ' for Nao.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.addressee: the audience (stage patter in a manzai act, with the pc as straight man)
findings.text: 昨日はね、箸を渡って、橋でご飯を食べました。
findings.en: Yesterday I crossed the chopsticks and ate my rice with a bridge.
findings.kansai: 昨日はな、箸を渡って、橋でご飯食べたねん。
findings.why: In the Kansai version, 食べたねん is a typical non-native form: Osaka speech says 食べてん or 食べたんや. The Kansai version also drops the polite stage register of the standard line (食べました). The same 〜たねん error appears in this part at mp.rehearsal#51ee79e0f0 and kr.makeup#fc506a8eae, and elsewhere in dialect/kansai_70_company, kansai_96_ko, kansai_99_returns and kansai_99_yn.
findings.direction: Correct the past-tense explanatory form throughout the Kansai files, and choose the act's register; e.g. '…橋でご飯食べましてん' (keeps the stage politeness) or '…食べてん'.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.addressee: pc and the troupe (after the rehearsal comes back to life)
findings.text: 鉛筆で書き込んだ名前は、消えてもまた書けるわ。役者は、そうやって生きてきたのよ。
findings.en: A name pencilled in can be written again if it fades. That's how actors have always lived.
findings.kansai: 鉛筆で書き込んだ名前は、消えてもまた書けるやん。役者は、そうやって生きてきたねんで。
findings.why: In the Kansai version, 生きてきたねんで uses the non-native 〜たねん form. A native Kansai voice actor would stumble on it or silently correct it.
findings.direction: Use a native past explanatory form; e.g. '…そうやって生きてきてんで' or '…生きてきたんやで'.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.addressee: pc (close companion, making up after a quarrel)
findings.text: ……さっきは、悪かったわ。野暮なんて、言うつもりじゃなかったの。手紙は、まだ怖くて開けないだけ。
findings.en: …Sorry about earlier. I didn't mean to call you rude. It's only that I'm still too scared to answer the letter.
findings.kansai: ……さっきは、悪かったな。野暮なんて、言うつもりちゃうかったねん。手紙は、まだ怖くて開けへんだけや。
findings.why: In the Kansai version, ちゃうかったねん is the non-native 〜たねん form in one of Suzu's tender apology lines. The dialect style sheet ranks emotional scenes first for native review.
findings.direction: e.g. '言うつもりやなかってん' or '言うつもりちゃうかってん'. (Side note outside register: the English says 'answer' but the Japanese says 開けない, 'open'.)

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: わたし、毎朝走っています。……夢の中で。
findings.en: I go for a run every morning. …In my dreams.
findings.kansai: うち、毎朝走ってるねん。……夢の中で。
findings.why: The standard act is consistent polite stage patter (いい天気ですね / 持って来ました / 走っています / 食べました). The Kansai act keeps 持って来ました but switches to plain in its other lines (ええ天気やね, 走ってるねん, 食べたねん), so its register wobbles inside a single routine. The style sheet says polite stage speech stays polite.
findings.direction: Pick one stage register for the whole Kansai routine; polite Kansai patter is available, e.g. '毎朝走ってますねん'.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.addressee: Sakutarō (stranger, a fellow actor in distress)
findings.text: 名前がなくても、台詞は体が覚えているわ。一緒に、読んでみましょう。
findings.en: Your body remembers the lines, even without the name. Let's read them together.
findings.kansai: 名前がなくても、台詞は体が覚えてるで。一緒に、読んでみよか。
findings.why: The standard line closes on a gentle polite invitation to a stranger (読んでみましょう). The Kansai version makes it plain (読んでみよか), so the dialect changes the politeness level.
findings.direction: Keep the polite softening in Kansai; e.g. '一緒に、読んでみましょか'.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: 幕を下ろしに行きましょう。……今度は、私たちの手で。
findings.en: Let's go and bring the curtain down. …With our own hands, this time.
findings.kansai: 幕を下ろしに行こ。……今度は、うちらの手で。
findings.why: Suzu is normally plain with the pc. Here the standard line deliberately rises to 〜ましょう for a solemn closing beat. The Kansai 行こ flattens that to everyday casual, so the dialect loses the register lift.
findings.direction: Keep the raised register in Kansai; e.g. '幕を下ろしに行きましょ'.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.addressee: pc (companion, wry, after a failed puzzle)
findings.text: 鐘は幕切れの合図。途中で鳴らしたら、芝居は終わっちゃうわ。
findings.en: The bell is the curtain. Ring it in the middle and the play's over.
findings.kansai: 鐘は幕切れの合図や。途中で鳴らしたら、芝居は終わってしまうで。
findings.why: The standard line uses the casual contraction 終わっちゃう. The Kansai version un-contracts it to 終わってしまうで, which sounds stiff in casual Osaka speech. The style sheet itself lists てまう.
findings.direction: e.g. '…芝居は終わってまうで'.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: ……ありがと。相方があなたでよかったわ。
findings.en: …Thanks. I'm glad you're my partner.
findings.kansai: ……おおきに。相方があんたでよかったわ。
findings.why: docs/dialect/suzu_kansai.md lists おおきに among the stock forms 'avoided as caricature', but the unit test allows up to 2, and both uses are in this part (here and mp.manzai#b07d0c8fcf). After a stage bow, おおきに can pass as theatrical. In a quiet apology it may sound like a costume rather than her voice.
findings.direction: Robin's call: either update the style sheet, or use plain ありがと here (ordinary in Osaka speech) and keep おおきに for the stage moment only.

findings.speaker: sousuke
findings.addressee: pc (known traveller; Sousuke's relationship with the pc is otherwise uniformly polite)
findings.text: 届け先の分からない手紙が一通あってね。最後の一行が消えていた。
findings.en: There's a letter here I couldn't deliver. Its last line had faded away.
findings.why: Sousuke's other ~30 lines to the pc are です/ます with dry jokes, including kr.lw_sb_ridgepost_sousuke and ko.lw_sb_dead_letters_open, which are adjacent in time. This scene, together with c071716558 (…読めるようになった。届けられるよ。), is entirely plain for no reason in the moment. That removes a character-specific politeness.
findings.direction: Restore his polite voice in both lines; e.g. '届け先の分からない手紙が一通ありましてね' / '…届けられますよ'.

findings.speaker: asahi
findings.text: これで港の連中も、箱を投げないだろうよ。
findings.en: Maybe now the dock lot will stop throwing them about.
findings.why: Asahi's ~30 other lines are bright and chatty (〜だよね, 〜の, うち) with no だろう. The gruff 〜だろうよ makes her sound like an old dockhand. This is a voice drift, not a gender rule.
findings.direction: Keep her usual lively casual; e.g. 'これで港の人たちも、箱を投げなくなるよね'.

findings.speaker: mp_manbe
findings.addressee: pc (helper the theatre is indebted to)
findings.text: 見てくれ、古い番付だ！「満員御礼」の字が、いつの間にか戻っていた。
findings.en: Look at this, an old playbill! "Full house, with thanks": the words came back when nobody was looking.
findings.why: Manbē asks the pc with 見てください elsewhere (mp.manbe_under, yn.lw_mp_curtain_open). His parallel good-news line in kr.lw_mp_manbe_play ends 大入り間違いなしです！ Here it is 見てくれ … and the next line (6b3df1f291) ends 満員間違いなしだ！ His plain exclamations are fine, but a plain request to the pc is not his pattern.
findings.direction: Keep the showman's polite core with plain exclamations; e.g. '見てください、古い番付です！' / '…満員間違いなしです！'.

findings.speaker: co_ume
findings.text: 干し場の札に、「干し柿」って字が戻ったのよ。孫が書いてくれた札なの。
findings.en: The tag on my drying rack: "Dried persimmons" is back on it. My grandchild wrote that tag for me.
findings.why: Grandma Ume's other 37 lines are folksy (〜だよ, 〜さ, 〜かい, お行き) and she never uses 〜のよ / 〜なの. Here she sounds like a different, younger standard-feminine speaker. The ko.back_* round as a whole reads as batch-written (see also Sousuke, Asahi, Manbē).
findings.direction: Return her to her own endings; e.g. '…字が戻ったんだよ。孫が書いてくれた札さ'.

findings.speaker: ren
findings.text: 蛾の夜、この灯を入れたのはあなたです。……あなたが、その「次の人」だったんですね。
findings.en: The night of the moths, you were the one who lit this lamp. …You were that "whoever came next".
findings.why: あなた twice in two short sentences to a close companion sounds like a rendering of English 'you…you'. The first あなた carries focus and is fine. The second can be dropped without loss.
findings.direction: Keep the focused first あなた and drop the second; e.g. '……その「次の人」だったんですね'.

findings.speaker: ren
findings.addressee: Ao (sulky boy, ashamed he cannot read)
findings.text: 拾う人がいるから、読む人が読めるのですよ。
findings.en: If no one picked them up, no one could read them.
findings.why: Ren's politeness is right, but 〜のですよ, spelled out in full, appears nowhere else in Ren's game lines. To an embarrassed child it sounds like a sermon rather than comfort.
findings.direction: Keep Ren polite and make it warmer; e.g. '…読む人が読めるんですよ'.

findings.speaker: mio
findings.text: ツルさんの言葉と、同じ……。昔の昔から、同じことがあったの？
findings.en: The same as Tsuru's words… Has this been happening since long, long ago?
findings.why: 昔の昔 is not a set phrase; it reads like a word-for-word rendering of 'long, long ago'. A surprised speaker would say そんな昔から or ずっと昔から (昔々 belongs to folktale openings).
findings.direction: e.g. 'そんな昔から、同じことがあったの？'.

findings.speaker: mp_vb_ginta
findings.text: 飼い主が来るまで、ここで待っている。三毛だから、ミケって呼んでいるの。
findings.en: I'll wait here till the owner comes. It's three colours, so I'm calling it Mike.
findings.why: A small boy using full 〜ている twice sounds read aloud, and his previous line is colloquial (この子でしょ？). The same pattern appears in kr.lw_sl_kr_sora_r3#35fff8e6d9 (石の字を写しているんだ). Other children in this part do contract (見てるの, 拾ってるだけ).
findings.direction: Use the spoken contraction; e.g. '…ここで待ってる。三毛だから、ミケって呼んでるんだ'.

findings.speaker: kr_hisae
findings.addressee: pc (younger traveller she has come to trust)
findings.text: 峠の道も、明るくなった。灯落へお行き。灯の名前を、忘れるんじゃないよ。
findings.en: The road over the pass is light now too. Go on to Lanternfall. And don't forget the lamps' names.
findings.why: Hisae's elder-to-younger commands are exactly right, but they are marked old-fashioned forms a learner may misread: お行き looks like honorific お〜, and おくれ / おやり / おいで / 使いな are unfamiliar. Other instances: kr.hisae_idle#60ebe5c14e (FROZEN VA2: 気をつけてお行き), kr.hisae_night#916f6e90db (迎えに行っておやり), #2064fec34a (仲直りしておいで), kr.hisae_inkstone#3033ea73f4 and kr.hisae_first#ca0cb1bce2 (〜ておくれ, 使いな).
findings.direction: No text change. Add one register note: お + verb stem as a warm, old-fashioned command from an elder to someone younger; おくれ = くれ; not a model for the learner's own speech.

findings.speaker: kr_kame
findings.text: 昔、罠にかかった子狐を、灯守が助けた。その夜、狐が一晩で橋を架けて、お礼をしたんだとさ。
findings.en: Long ago a keeper freed a fox cub from a snare. That night the foxes built the bridge in a single night, to say thank you. So the story goes.
findings.why: The folktale hearsay ending 〜とさ ('so they say') is right for a teller. Learners will not have met it and may parse it as と + さ. It recurs in kr.kikyo_lodge#56879f26f0 (開いたとさ) and mp.lw_sg_kiyo_traders#89748a2769 (売ってるんだとさ).
findings.direction: No text change. Add a note: 〜とさ / 〜んだとさ is a casual hearsay or storyteller's ending, like 〜そうだ.

findings.speaker: any (actually suzu: the scene ends for comp!=suzu)
findings.text: ……あら。懐かしい。わたし、こんなに小さい字だったのね。
findings.en: …Oh. How it takes me back. My name was this small.
findings.why: This is a recording-pipeline risk, not a script problem. The voice line list gives speaker 'any' and kansai: null for all three stagedoor lines, which are Suzu only, and for the companion-branched mp.fireworks lines. It also gives kansai: null for mp.tokube#443558e52e. Yet src/content/dialect/kansai_94_mp.js has Kansai versions of the stagedoor lines, the six Suzu fireworks lines and the tokube line, so Kansai takes could go unrecorded or be cast to the wrong voice.
findings.direction: Attribute these lines by branch (fireworks :nao/:mio/:ren/:suzu; stagedoor = Suzu) and attach their Kansai variants before building the recording scripts.

findings.speaker: cr_jinpachi
findings.addressee: pc (stranger, first meeting; relaying a message from Lanternfall's council)
findings.text: でも、「直接来てください」ってところは確かです！ヤエさんが言っていました。
findings.en: But the part about "please come in person", that's certain! Yae said it.
findings.why: The Lanternfall councillor who sends this message is speaker lf_yae, whose display name everywhere else is タミ (Councillor Tami: ch5/05_cast.js, ch5/22_main.js '議員のタミですよ'). ヤエ is the Snowbell innkeeper from ch4, so the recording would name the wrong person. The cr script seems to have taken the speaker id as her name.
findings.direction: Use the councillor's in-game name, e.g. 'タミさんが言っていました'. The same fix is needed in cr.call#d3b1320685 (Mio), in cr_kanbe's line '灯落のヤエさんから…' (cr/20_scenes_call.js:111, p10) and in the cr journal/quest text (cr/06_quests.js:12, cr/20_scenes_call.js:46).

findings.speaker: mio
findings.text: 大事なところが、抜けてしまったみたいですね。ヤエさんに直接聞きましょう。
findings.en: The important part seems to have dropped out. Let's ask Yae herself.
findings.why: Same naming error: the person they go to ask is Councillor Tami (タミ), not ヤエ. Mio is also polite to the player here; see the cr Mio register findings.
findings.direction: Rename to タミさん. The register should follow whatever is decided for Mio in cr (see cr.arrive5#f1f1f8a13b).

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: ……「なぜかというと」の続き、書けなかったのよ。今も、書けない。
findings.en: …I couldn't write what came after "The reason is". I still can't.
findings.kansai: ……「なぜかというと」の続き、書けへんかったねん。今も、書けへん。
findings.why: In Kansai, a past form takes ねん as 〜てん (書けへんかってん), or you can say 〜たんや. '書けへんかったねん' sounds non-native and a Kansai listener would notice it. The same 〜かったねん pattern also turns up in dialect/kansai_95_kr.js:66, kansai_70_company.js:222 and kansai_99_yn.js:37 and :136.
findings.direction: Use the contracted past, e.g. '書けへんかってん。今も、書けへん。' Check the other 〜かったねん / 〜たねん lines in the Kansai files the same way.

findings.speaker: mio
findings.text: 少し、息が苦しいです。高い所に来たからでしょう。無理はしないでくださいね。
findings.en: I'm a little short of breath. It must be the height. Don't push yourself.
findings.why: One chapter earlier (ko, ch9), Mio talks to the player in soft plain speech: 'ここで待ってるから、無理しないでね' (ko.tide_split), '怪我は？手、見せて' (ko.reunion). She was already plain in lf (ch5). In cr (ch10) she goes back to stranger-level です/ます with the same person and nothing in the story explains it. The same thing happens in cr.arrive1, arrive2, arrive3, arrive4, arrive6, barrier_first and bridge, and in p10's cr.family '重いことを決めましたね。一人で背負わないでください', which is almost word for word ko.kihei_choose '重いことを決めたわね。一人で背負わないで'.
findings.direction: Bring Mio's companion lines in cr into line with her established soft plain register towards the player. Keep です/ます where she addresses strangers (Chika, Ujie, Heisuke). e.g. '少し、息が苦しい。高いからかな。無理しないでね。'

findings.speaker: mio
findings.addressee: pc (companion, close; reunion after the player crossed the pass alone)
findings.text: おかえりなさい。頭も治りました。生姜の飴、役に立ちましたか？
findings.en: Welcome back. My head's better. Did the ginger sweet help?
findings.why: This is an emotional reunion, but she reports to the player as if to a customer. The parallel reunion one chapter earlier (ko.reunion) is warm plain speech ('……ごめん、泣いてないよ'). '頭も治りました' and '役に立ちましたか' sound distant from a close friend.
findings.direction: Use the soft plain register of her ko and lf lines. 'おかえり(なさい)' can stay. e.g. '頭も治ったよ。生姜の飴、役に立った？'

findings.speaker: mio
findings.addressee: pc (companion; alone together on an empty islet)
findings.text: 誰もいない島ですね。……たまには、いいです。
findings.en: An island with nobody on it. …Now and then, that's nice.
findings.why: This is a private, relaxed aside with nobody else there, yet it is in です/ます, and 'たまには、いいです' sounds stiff in that moment. In sg (the same harbour, ch2) Mio is mostly plain with the player. The sea/sz/el scenes can be played at any point from ch2 on, so they need a register that fits a friend.
findings.direction: Use a soft plain line, e.g. '誰もいない島……。たまには、いいね。'. Her other sea companion lines can stay polite where Tetsu, Kajirō, Fuku or Isaku are being addressed.

findings.speaker: ko_otoha
findings.text: 葉守は、古今集の序を唱えてきました。「やまとうたは、人の心を種として」……古い、本当の歌の本の言葉ですよ。
findings.en: The keepers have always recited the Kokinshū's preface. "Japanese poetry takes the human heart as its seed…" Words from an old book of poems: a real one.
findings.why: '本当の歌の本' is the designer telling the learner that the Kokinshū exists in real life. Inside the fantasy world the remark makes no sense ('a real book' as opposed to what?), and it sounds odd when spoken. This is a teaching note leaking into character speech.
findings.direction: Move the 'this is a real text' note to word help or the learning panel and let Otoha just place the text, e.g. '……古い歌の本の言葉です。'

findings.speaker: ko_tokio
findings.text: ……お願いがあります。今日の籠が、まだ二つ数えていません。
findings.en: …I have a favour to ask. Two of today's baskets haven't been counted yet.
findings.why: '籠が…数えていません' makes the baskets the subject of a transitive verb, so it reads as if the baskets haven't counted. Careless speech allows this, but it doesn't suit fussy, exact Tokio, and a native ear will catch it in a recording.
findings.direction: Make the baskets the object, or use a resultative form, e.g. '今日の籠を、まだ二つ数えていません' or 'まだ数えていない籠が、二つあります'.

findings.speaker: ko_tokio
findings.text: 段のアオの籠と、浜の籠です。数を教えてください。葉は一枚、二枚と数えます。
findings.en: Ao's basket on the terraces, and the one on the shore. Tell me the numbers. Leaves are counted 一枚, 二枚.
findings.why: In the game world any adult knows that leaves take 枚, so Tokio explaining the counter to the player is the grammar lesson speaking.
findings.direction: Put the counter reminder in the task UI or word help. If Tokio keeps a line, make it a fussy instruction rather than a definition, e.g. '一枚ずつ、正確にお願いします。'

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.addressee: pc (companion, close; being separated by the tide)
findings.text: ……大丈夫、幕間よ、幕間！次の幕で会いましょう。出番忘れたら、承知しないからね！
findings.en: …It's all right, it's just the interval! See you in the next act. Miss your cue and I'll never forgive you!
findings.kansai: ……大丈夫、幕間や、幕間！次の幕で会おう。出番忘れたら、承知せえへんで！
findings.why: In the standard line, '次の幕で会いましょう' is a stagey 〜ましょう flourish. The Kansai version changes it to plain '会おう', so the dialect switch also changes the register. The handling is uneven: cr.arrive2 '挨拶して行きましょ' becomes '行こ' and cr.call '見に行きましょ' becomes '見に行こ', but ko.kihei_ask keeps '探しましょう' in Kansai.
findings.direction: Keep the 〜ましょ(う) flavour in Kansai, which uses it naturally, e.g. '次の幕で会いましょ' or '会いましょか', and apply one rule to the three lines.

findings.speaker: pc
findings.addressee: Mina and Riku (hamlet children asking the player to be their teacher)
findings.text: 引き受けます。
findings.en: All right.
findings.why: This is the only 'yes' the player has. '引き受けます' is how you accept a commission from an adult, as the same choice works for Ōmi in sea.omi_deal. Said to a child who asked '先生になってくれる？', it sounds stiff and businesslike. The English 'All right.' is casual.
findings.direction: Give a child-appropriate acceptance, e.g. 'いいよ。' or 'うん、やろう。'. Optionally offer a polite option next to it if the menu is meant to teach register.

findings.speaker: ren
findings.text: 灯の道でも、名前が消える速さは、年ごとに速くなっていました。
findings.en: On the lantern roads too, the names were fading faster every year.
findings.why: '速さは…速くなっていました' (the speed got speedier) is a clumsy repetition, and it is audible in a recording. Ren's precision should come across as exact wording, not this.
findings.direction: Remove the doubling, e.g. '名前が消えるのが、年ごとに速くなっていました' or '消える速さが、年ごとに増していました'.

findings.speaker: ko_gardener
findings.text: ここの葉は、届けてはならぬ言葉。書いた者が、出さぬと決めた言葉だ。
findings.en: The leaves here are words that must not be delivered. Their writers chose not to send them.
findings.why: The classical 〜ぬ (ならぬ, 出さぬ) belongs to this ageless keeper-spirit and is right for it. Learners meet it here with no note telling them it is the literary negative and not a model for everyday speech.
findings.direction: No text change. Add a register note: 〜ぬ = 〜ない, an old literary form used here for a spirit's voice.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.addressee: Nana and the village children (an impromptu audience)
findings.text: さあさあ、お立ち会い！言の葉島の、始まりの話！
findings.en: Roll up, roll up! The story of how Kotonoha began!
findings.why: 'お立ち会い' is a traditional street-performer's call, exactly right for Suzu. A learner can't parse it, and it isn't something to say in ordinary conversation.
findings.direction: No text change. Add a register note for the street-performer's call to the crowd.

findings.speaker: sz_yone
findings.addressee: pc (stranger, asked for help by an elder)
findings.text: 若い目を貸しておくれ。破れた目を見つけて、繕い方を一緒に。
findings.en: Lend me young eyes. Find the torn meshes, and we'll mend them together.
findings.why: '〜ておくれ' is an older speaker's affectionate request form, and it fits Yone. It appears again in sz.yone_nets ('言っておくれ'). Learners need to know it is a marked elderly form of 〜てくれ.
findings.direction: No text change. Add a register note on おくれ.

findings.speaker: cr_gonza
findings.addressee: pc and companion (travellers at a checkpoint)
findings.text: 待たれよ。手形の改めは、番所で。
findings.en: Halt. Papers are checked in the office.
findings.why: '待たれよ' is archaic, period-drama guard speech. It is a deliberate trait of Gonza ('stiff guard speech'), but the scene gives no hint that it is stylized and not current Japanese.
findings.direction: No text change. Add a note: archaic official imperative, roughly 待ってください / 止まれ.

findings.speaker: cr_jinpachi
findings.text: おいら、継ぎ飛脚のジンパチです。伝言は、宿場から宿場へ、口で伝えて来ました。
findings.en: I'm Jinpachi, a relay runner. The message came station to station, by word of mouth.
findings.why: 'おいら' with です/ます is a deliberate character blend: a rustic, boyish errand-runner trying to be polite. Learners need to know おいら is a marked, old-fashioned casual 'I' and not a neutral pronoun.
findings.direction: No text change. Add a register note on おいら.

findings.speaker: cr_jinpachi
findings.text: おいらは先に戻ります！灯の道の上の端、追分の宿にいますんで！
findings.en: I'll head back ahead of you! I'll be at Oiwake Station, at the top end of the Lantern Road!
findings.why: 'いますんで' (polite verb + casual んで, short for ので) is natural, chatty speech, but beginners will not have met this mix.
findings.direction: No text change. Word help should give んで = ので.

findings.speaker: el_genroku
findings.addressee: pc (helper he has grown to trust)
findings.text: 朝に掃いて、昼に鐘を鳴らす。……忙しくなったわい。
findings.en: Sweep in the morning, ring the bell at noon. …I've got busy.
findings.why: Sentence-final わい (also in el.lw_el_genroku_winter '落ち着かなかったわい'), together with わし and ふん, is strong old-man role language. It fits gruff Genroku, and his lines avoid じゃ, so it is not overdone. A learner would still take わい for a normal ending.
findings.direction: No text change. Add a register note on わい/わし as an elderly male speech style.

findings.speaker: ko_hamaji
findings.text: ミツの汁は、何年食っても飽きん。……本人には言うなよ。
findings.en: Years of Mitsu's soup and I'm not tired of it. …Don't tell her I said so.
findings.why: The 〜ん negative (飽きん, and '見ておかんと' in ko.lw_sl_ko_hamaji_r2; Kajirō's '急がん', Tetsu's '要らん' in the sea scenes) suits these old seamen, but a learner may not recognise it as 〜ない.
findings.direction: No text change. Word help or a register note should give 〜ん = 〜ない (older or rougher speech).

findings.speaker: cr_sono
findings.addressee: pc (traveller at her inn; possibly a stranger: the table prop has no cr_sono_met condition)
findings.text: それね。商人のお客さんが置いて行ったの。誰のかしら。
findings.en: That one? A merchant left it. I wonder whose it is.
findings.why: Sono speaks quiet です/ます to the player in every other line (cr.sono, cr.family, cr.family_sono, cr.saka_shelf, cr.sono_after: 祖父が建てた宿です, 話してあげてください). Only here, at the guest-book table in her own inn, does she switch to chatty feminine plain (〜の, かしら), and this can be the first thing she ever says to the player.
findings.direction: Bring the guest-book lines into her polite register, keeping them light; e.g. 「それですか。商人のお客さんが置いて行ったんです。」

findings.speaker: cr_sono
findings.text: 松葉の紋……中山の松葉屋さんのね。コウスケさんが置いて行ったのよ。持って行ってあげて。
findings.en: A pine-needle crest… the Matsuba's, at Nakayama. Kōsuke left it here. Take it back to them.
findings.why: This is the same problem as #8822c6328a: のよ and the plain request 持って行ってあげて, where everywhere else she says 話してあげてください to the same person. The VA would be voicing two different Sonos.
findings.direction: Use the same polite level as her other scenes; e.g. 「…持って行ってあげてください。」

findings.speaker: cr_kanbe
findings.addressee: pc (newcomer sent by the Lanternfall council)
findings.text: 灯落のヤエさんから、話は聞いている。本当に来たのか。
findings.en: I've had word from Yae in Lanternfall. So you really came.
findings.why: The councillor who sends the player here is speaker lf_yae, whose display name is タミ (Councillor Tami: ch5/05_cast.js; she introduces herself as 議員のタミです in ch5). Here Kanbe calls her ヤエさん, as do Jinpachi and Mio in cr.call and the cr journal. ヤエ is also a different character, the Snowbell innkeeper in ch4. Recorded as written, the councillor gets a second name.
findings.direction: Decide the councillor's name once (the nameplate says タミ) and make Kanbe's line, cr.call and the journal match it before recording.

findings.speaker: cr_heisuke
findings.text: 次は中山のオタキに、わしから頼む。「雨がやんだら、大工を寄越してほしい。橋を直す。」
findings.en: Next, from me, to Otaki at Nakayama: "Once the rain stops, send us carpenters. We'll fix the bridge."
findings.why: Heisuke says 俺 every other time he refers to himself (俺の親父が始めた話だ, それが、俺の仕事だ, 俺も、親父の話を…) and わし only here, to the same player in the same arc. A first-person switch is very audible in recording.
findings.direction: Choose one pronoun for Heisuke. 俺 fits his other lines; e.g. 「…俺から頼む。」

findings.speaker: nao
findings.text: ……決めた。答えは、サキチさんに直接言う。手紙じゃなくてな。
findings.en: …I've decided. I'll give Sakichi my answer in person. Not by letter.
findings.why: The next line opens with 手紙は書いた, and Nao then hand-delivers that letter (cr.nao_evening, cr.porch_nao). Heard aloud, 'not by letter' followed by 'I wrote the letter' is a contradiction. The intended contrast is 'not only by letter / not hiding behind a letter'.
findings.direction: Make the contrast explicit; e.g. 「手紙だけじゃなくてな。」 or let the next line concede 「手紙も、書いたけど。」

findings.speaker: nao
findings.addressee: pc (companion, who has just apologised to Heisuke)
findings.text: 聞いたと言えば、聞いた話になる。言わなければ、見た話になる。……覚えておけ。
findings.en: Say you heard it, and it's a thing you heard. Don't, and it becomes a thing you saw. …Remember that.
findings.why: Heisuke has just said 気にするな. Nao then recites the arc's lesson as a balanced maxim and finishes with an order to memorise it, which reads as the tutorial talking. Nao is wry and impatient with ceremony and elsewhere makes the point in one dry line.
findings.direction: Keep the point but make it Nao's aside rather than a lesson to memorise: shorter, wry, without 覚えておけ; e.g. 「次は『聞いた』って付けろ。それだけで済む。」

findings.speaker: pc
findings.addressee: Genji (elderly horse-driver; the player's bad message sent him onto a blocked ledge)
findings.text: すみません。地図の話だけを伝えてしまった。
findings.en: Sorry. I passed on only the map's side.
findings.why: Every other apology choice in these consequence scenes is fully polite (r2, r5, and the first r4 option 分けて言うべきでした). This one starts with すみません and ends with plain しまった, which sounds like muttering to yourself rather than apologising to an elder. It is neither a clean casual option nor a polite one.
findings.direction: Make it one register: polite to match the menu (e.g. 「…伝えてしまいました。」) or, if a casual option is wanted, casual throughout.

findings.speaker: pc
findings.addressee: Ujie (barrier keeper, formal official) or the companion; Ujie is the one who answers
findings.text: 一緒に行けないのか。
findings.en: We can't go together?
findings.why: The player has just passed cr.interview, which teaches formal です/ます answers to this same keeper, and Ujie replies to this choice with 申し訳ございません. A blunt plain question to him undercuts the lesson. If the line is meant for the companion, the scene does not show that.
findings.direction: Either offer a polite version addressed to Ujie (e.g. 「一緒に行けないんですか。」) or make clear the line is said to the companion.

findings.speaker: nao
findings.addressee: Oshika (old pilgrim, met just before) and pc
findings.text: ……南の島の話。願いじゃない。出せなかった手紙だ。海は叶えない。返すだけだ。
findings.en: …That island in the south. Not wishes: letters that never got sent. The sea doesn't grant them. It only gives them back.
findings.why: In this conversation Oshika only asks for a rubbing. Her island story is in the earlier encounter's exit text (cr.wander_oshika leave), so all four companion replies (#2643376a13, #66c9411ba1, #309a939c48, #6b83e87854) answer something not said in this exchange. Heard as a scene, it is a non sequitur.
findings.direction: Give Oshika a one-line callback in this scene (her wish to see the island one day) before the companions answer it, or have the companions name the earlier story.

findings.speaker: ren
findings.text: 灯も、一晩ごとに芯を切ります。守りも、一回ごとに新しくできるかもしれません。
findings.en: Lamps too: you trim the wick every night. A ward could be made new every time, too, perhaps.
findings.why: The second sentence is the battle modifier's own wording (encounters/10_modifiers.js: 一回ごとに守る), dropped into a chat about relay runners. 守り has no referent in the conversation, so it reads as a tutorial hint in Ren's mouth, stacked onto a second textbook ごとに sentence.
findings.direction: Keep Ren's lamp-wick observation as the ごとに example. Move the ward hint to the challenge or make it a natural thought of Ren's, not a mechanic.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: 十六の時、彼の間の取り方を、毎晩真似したの。一座の皆に、似てないって笑われたけど。
findings.en: When I was sixteen I copied his timing every night. Everyone in the troupe laughed and said it was nothing like him.
findings.why: In casual talk about her idol, 彼 sounds like it comes from English 'his'. A speaker would say あの人の or use his name.
findings.direction: Replace 彼 with a spoken reference; e.g. 「あの人の間の取り方を」 (the Kansai line likewise).

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: 十六の時、彼の間の取り方を、毎晩真似したの。一座の皆に、似てないって笑われたけど。
findings.en: When I was sixteen I copied his timing every night. Everyone in the troupe laughed and said it was nothing like him.
findings.kansai: 十六の時、彼の間の取り方を、毎晩真似したねん。一座の皆に、似てへんって笑われたけど。
findings.why: 真似したねん (past + ねん) is not native Osaka speech; the past explanatory form is 真似してん / 真似したんや. The project's own guide sample (docs/dialect/suzu_kansai.md) uses 言うてみたかってん. A Kansai listener will hear 〜たねん as imitation Kansai. About a dozen 〜たねん forms appear in the dialect files.
findings.direction: Use the contracted past explanatory; e.g. 「…毎晩真似してん。」

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: ああ……極楽、極楽。一度言ってみたかったの。
findings.en: Ahh… paradise, paradise. I always wanted to say that.
findings.kansai: ああ……極楽、極楽。一回言うてみたかったねん。
findings.why: Same 〜たねん error as yn.bath_beat#19abc2bc96: 言うてみたかったねん. The dialect guide's own example of this exact joke is いっぺん言うてみたかってん.
findings.direction: e.g. 「一回言うてみたかってん。」

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.addressee: Oritsu and Tahei (two quarrelling innkeepers, strangers), in public
findings.text: 幕を下ろして！二人とも、客席を見なさいよ。皆、怖がっているわ。
findings.en: Bring the curtain down! Both of you, look at your audience. Everyone's frightened.
findings.kansai: 幕を下ろして！二人とも、客席を見て。皆、怖がってるやん。
findings.why: The standard line is an angry scolding command (見なさいよ). The Kansai version turns it into a plain request (見て), so Suzu's anger is softened in dialect only. The politeness level is the same, but the force of the line is not.
findings.direction: Keep the scolding command in Kansai; e.g. 「客席見ぃや。」

findings.speaker: cr_gonza
findings.text: 通られよ。峠は雪だ。気をつけて。
findings.en: Pass. There's snow on the pass. Take care.
findings.why: 〜られよ (archaic honorific imperative, a guard's set phrase) is the line's key word, and no lexicon or word-help entry explains it. Learners will not connect it to 通る or know it is stylized.
findings.direction: Add a word-help/register note: 通られよ = old formal 'you may pass', a gate-guard's set phrase, not modern speech. No text change.

findings.speaker: cr_seibe
findings.text: 竹屋でござる。向かいの松葉屋より、風呂が熱い。
findings.en: This is the Take. Our bath is hotter than the Matsuba's across the way.
findings.why: Seibe's comic でござる (also cr.lw_sl_cr_seibe_r2/_r3) and タツどの (cr.seibe#cae41b9a67) are deliberate archaisms with no note. Word help currently splits ござる as the ご- prefix. Learners need to know this is a joke-archaic voice, not a polite model.
findings.direction: Add a register note: でござる = samurai-drama 'it is', used here for comic effect; どの = old 'Mr/Master'. Keep the lines.

findings.speaker: yn_bunkichi
findings.text: 一行でも、集まったら聞かせておくれ。
findings.en: Even one line: when you have it, let me hear.
findings.why: 〜ておくれ (old, warm request form) together with でござい, おいでだね and ありがとうよ makes up Bunkichi's patter. ござい has a lexicon entry; おくれ has none anywhere in the lexicons.
findings.direction: Add a note: 〜ておくれ = old-fashioned, affectionate 'please do … for me' (≈ 〜てくれ / 〜てください), an elder's or tradesman's voice.

findings.speaker: cr_oshika
findings.addressee: pc (traveller who helped her on the shrine path)
findings.text: 最後の一つが、雲路峠の石じゃ。じゃが、この足では、雲の上までは登れん。
findings.en: The last is the stone on the Cloudroad Pass. But with these legs I can't climb above the cloud.
findings.why: Oshika is the only heavy じゃ/じゃが/からの/くれんか speaker in the part. This is the stock 'old person' role language (老人語), and it sits next to a standard 先ほどはどうも. It works as a pilgrim's colour, but learners get no note that this is a stylized elder voice and not dialect or a model to copy.
findings.direction: Add a register note on じゃ (= だ), じゃが (= だが), 〜からの (= からね), くれんか (= くれないか) as an elder's stylized speech. Keep her voice as it is.

findings.speaker: lf_setsu
findings.text: 「沸いておりません」と、ちゃんと申し上げていますわ。
findings.en: "It is not," I tell them. Properly.
findings.why: Setsu's ですわ / ますの (also #8d4ede5804 聞かれますの) is the stylized 'refined young lady' ending, rare in real speech today. As her character colour it is fine, but a learner will take it for ordinary polite feminine speech.
findings.direction: Add a register note: 〜ますの / 〜ですわ = old-fashioned refined feminine, a character voice; everyday polite speech is 〜ます / 〜です.

findings.speaker: cr_jinpachi
findings.text: 峠までは、駕籠もありますから！雲居まで、乗ってってください。
findings.en: There's the palanquin as far as Kumoi! Ride it up.
findings.why: 乗ってって = 乗っていって with the い dropped. The double て is hard to parse, and it comes in a key story beat. Natural for chatty Jinpachi.
findings.direction: Make sure word help glosses 乗ってって as 乗っていって ('take it and go'). No text change.

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: 灯が全部点いたら、ほどけるんだろう。
findings.en: I expect it unties once all the lights are lit.
findings.why: Plain conjecture with 〜んだろう is Nao's voice. Ren never speaks plain to the player (none of Ren's ~280 lines uses だろう, みたいだ or a plain volitional), and Mio and Suzu would say 〜んでしょう / 〜んでしょ. Recorded by Ren's actor, it sounds out of character.
findings.direction: Either give each companion its own line, or use an ending all four can say, e.g. 'ほどけるのかも'. The same applies to the existing Kansai variant ほどけるんやろな.

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: 順番が違ったみたいだ。札をもう一度読もう。
findings.en: Wrong order, it seems. Let's read the note again.
findings.why: The same line plays in l8_E, l8_N, l8_S and l8_W. 〜みたいだ。 plus the plain volitional 読もう fits Nao only. Ren would say 違ったようです／読みましょう, and Mio and Suzu would drop the だ (違ったみたい／みたいね).
findings.direction: Write per-companion variants, or at least drop the だ so the line is not marked as Nao's; Ren needs a polite form.

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: 並び順が分からなくて、困っているみたいだ。
findings.en: They seem stuck: nobody knows the order to walk in.
findings.why: This has the same 〜みたいだ。 ending as the l8 line. It is natural from Nao, slightly masculine-neutral from Mio or Suzu, and wrong for Ren, who would say 困っているようです.
findings.direction: Use per-companion lines, or an ending that suits all four, e.g. '困っているみたい'. Ren still needs a polite variant.

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: 地図の通りだ。読んで、歩いて、見つけた。
findings.en: Just as the map said. Read it, walked it, found it.
findings.why: The same line appears in t6_sw. The だ exclamation and clipped verb list fit Nao well and Suzu passably. Mio would say 地図の通りね and Ren 地図の通りです.
findings.direction: Give Ren a polite variant, and consider softer endings for Mio.

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: 全部、どこかで一度習ったことだ。忘れてないものだね。
findings.en: Every one of them something we learned somewhere along the way. We haven't forgotten.
findings.why: This mixes a blunt plain 〜ことだ。 with a soft 〜ものだね, so it suits no single companion cleanly, and it is plain, which Ren never uses. It also recaps the lesson aloud.
findings.direction: Pick one register per speaker. A Ren variant needs です/ます.

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: 角を数え直してみようか。入り口から、もう一度。
findings.en: Shall we count the corners again? From the way in, once more.
findings.why: This one is systemic: all 51 ANY(comp) lines in the Hall are plain, and none has a companion branch. The plain volitional and ね lines suit Nao, Mio and Suzu, but not Ren, whose speech is careful polite. Examples: this one (l4_e6/e13/e20/w6/w13/w20), f2_first#cca42afdbd 歩こう, t4_card#dc2b933197 行こう, t6_ne#1bca7b3af0 and k_*#8b053ac2bd 言おうか？, w2.l4_*#3b36a99fe5 読もう, w10.t2_board#866bb5acc3, w2.t4_card#5a7df36726, st*#556dcc75aa, pg4#086b677972.
findings.direction: Decide whether a Ren-specific polite variant is generated for ANY lines (e.g. '数え直してみましょうか'). Otherwise every Hall prompt from Ren drops Ren's register.

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: 道を聞くのも、断るのも、人の話を伝えるのも、全部この館で練習したんだね。
findings.en: Asking the way, saying no, passing on what someone said: we practised all of it in this Hall.
findings.why: This plays after each of the nine to_w* placements. The companion lists the curriculum back to the player, which is a teaching summary in character speech, and it repeats in every scene that reaches :all.
findings.direction: Shorten it to a reaction rather than a syllabus, or let the narration carry the recap.

findings.speaker: nao
findings.text: 全体か。一人ずつじゃなく、丸ごと。……守る時にも、使える言葉だな。
findings.en: As a whole. Not one by one: all of it. …A word you could use when you're protecting people, too.
findings.why: Before [teach mod_zentai], every companion comments on the everyday word 全体 as if meeting it for the first time. Nao calls it 'a word you can use', and Ren (#7bb3da1ca6) ends with ……覚えました. Native speakers do not remark on a common word like this, so the vocabulary lesson leaks into speech. Mio's and Suzu's lines, which apply the idea, are fine.
findings.direction: Let Nao and Ren react to the idea (the valley as one body) rather than to the word, and leave the vocabulary point to the teach card.

findings.speaker: nao
findings.text: 時計は直った。半日ずつ分けて、明日の朝出ればいい。全員に口を出させたら、誰も何も得ないぞ。
findings.en: The clock's fixed. Split it half a day each and we leave in the morning. Let everyone have their say and nobody gets anything.
findings.why: 誰も何も得ない is a word-for-word 'nobody gets anything'. 得ない (えない) is bookish in an angry casual line and can also be heard as the auxiliary 〜得ない ('cannot'), which risks a misreading on recording.
findings.direction: Use a spoken idiom for 'it gets nobody anywhere', e.g. '誰の得にもならないぞ' or 'まとまるものもまとまらないぞ'.

findings.speaker: nao
findings.text: ……静かだ。俺の足音が、自分に聞こえない。
findings.en: …Quiet. I can't hear my own footsteps.
findings.why: 俺の … 自分に refers to the same person twice in one short clause; it is 'my own footsteps aren't audible to myself' rendered literally. A speaker would say 自分の足音も聞こえない. It may be meant to echo Yasuke's 自分の声も、自分に聞こえない (#b7bf846619), which is acceptable as his stunned phrasing, but in Nao's mouth it sounds translated.
findings.direction: Drop either 俺の or 自分に, e.g. '自分の足音も聞こえない'.

findings.speaker: nao
findings.text: 紙に書いたか。……正しい。声が届かないなら、紙だ。
findings.en: You wrote it down. …Right call. If your voice won't carry, use paper.
findings.why: A bare ……正しい。 as an approving interjection is 'Correct.' translated. Japanese speakers say それでいい / 正解だ / いい判断だ. Read flat, it sounds robotic rather than wry.
findings.direction: Use a natural approving reply, e.g. '……それでいい。'.

findings.speaker: nao
findings.text: 全員の話を聞くってのは、座って待つってことだ。……俺が一番苦手なことを、お前はやろうとしていた。それが、腹が立ったんだと思う。
findings.en: Hearing everyone out means sitting and waiting. …You were about to do the thing I'm worst at. I think that's what made me angry.
findings.why: それが、腹が立った shapes 'that is what made me angry' with が, where speech uses に or で (それに腹が立った / それで腹が立った). The hedge 〜んだと思う at the end reads like 'I think'. The rest of the line is good Nao.
findings.direction: Fix the particle and make the hedge sound like Nao, e.g. 'たぶん、それで腹が立ったんだ'.

findings.speaker: mio
findings.text: ……昨夜は、ごめんなさい。「大丈夫」と言って、扉を閉めました。一人で決めたかった。でも、待たせる必要はなかった。
findings.en: …I'm sorry about last night. I said "I'm fine" and shut the door on you. I wanted to decide by myself. But there was no need to keep you waiting.
findings.why: 待たせる必要はなかった is 'there was no need to keep you waiting', with 必要 used as in English. A spoken apology would be 待たせることはなかった or 待たせなくてもよかったのに. Also, 扉 is a hinged door, while the scene closed a 戸; the figurative sense still works.
findings.direction: Use a spoken regret form, e.g. '待たせることなんて、なかったのに'.

findings.speaker: mio
findings.text: 耳が、また詰まります。……大丈夫。進みましょう。
findings.en: My ears are blocking up again. …I'm all right. Let's go on.
findings.why: The plain present 詰まります reports a sensation happening now as if it were a habit or forecast. People say 耳がまた詰まってきました or 詰まる感じがします.
findings.direction: Use 〜てきた or 〜感じ, e.g. 'また耳が詰まってきました'.

findings.speaker: nao
findings.addressee: pc (companion; amused aside about two lovers' hidden names)
findings.text: 石に彫るだけじゃ足りなかったわけか。愚かな二人だ。
findings.en: Carving it on the stone outside wasn't enough, then. A foolish pair.
findings.why: Nao is smirking fondly, but 愚か is a written, judging word. Aloud, 愚かな二人だ sounds like condemnation or oracle-speak rather than affectionate teasing. This is the only 愚か in the game's dialogue.
findings.direction: Use a fond colloquial word, e.g. 'しょうがない二人だな' or 'バカな二人だ'.

findings.speaker: as_mitsue
findings.text: 坂の上まで。松の下から、村中の灯が見えるわ。
findings.en: Right up the slope. From under the pine you'll see the whole village lit.
findings.why: This is one of three parallel results of the same choice. The other two are polite (明るくなりますね / 倍に見えますよ), and all 25 other Mitsue lines are です/ます, so the plain feminine 見えるわ in one branch has no reason.
findings.direction: Match the sibling branches, e.g. '村中の灯が見えますよ'.

findings.speaker: yn_oshige
findings.text: ……揉み歌。村で、稲刈りの後に歌った。最後の行は、「明日も歩ける、軽い足」。……村で、最後に歌ったのは、いつだったか。
findings.en: …The massage song. We sang it in the village after the rice harvest. The last line goes, "Light feet, to walk again tomorrow." …When did we last sing it in the village, I wonder.
findings.why: Oshige is gentle polite in her other four lines to the player (助かります, 看てもらいました, 帰ろうと思います). Here the whole answer is plain. The closing いつだったか works as a murmur to herself, but 歌った。最後の行は… is information given to the player.
findings.direction: Keep the murmured last sentence, and make the answer to the player polite, e.g. '稲刈りの後に歌いました'.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: ツルさん、帰りの道中、退屈はさせませんよ。
findings.en: Keeper Tsuru, I won't let you be bored on the way home.
findings.kansai: ツルさん、帰りの道中は、うちが盛り上げるで。
findings.why: The standard line is polite to an elder (させませんよ). The Kansai version is plain (盛り上げるで) and switches to うち, so choosing Kansai changes the politeness, which the dialect style sheet forbids.
findings.direction: Keep the polite ending in Kansai and change only the intonation or particle, e.g. '退屈はさせませんで'.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.addressee: the troupe (Shinza, Koume; family-like) and pc
findings.text: 帳尻は合っているって、皆に言ってきた。本当は、足りない分を、私の取り分から埋めていたの。嵐の後に残ったのも、町ごとの借金を返すため。
findings.en: I told everyone the books balanced. In truth I was covering the shortfall from my own share. When I stayed behind after the storm, it was to pay off the debts town by town.
findings.kansai: 帳尻は合うてるって、皆に言うてきた。ほんまは、足りへん分を、私の取り分から埋めてたねん。嵐の後に残ったのも、町ごとの借金を返すためや。
findings.why: Kansai 埋めてたねん puts ねん after a past form. Osaka speech uses 〜てん (埋めててん) or 〜たんや, and 〜たねん is a well-known marker of imitation Kansai. The game's own style sheet sample uses みたかってん. This is Suzu's emotional peak, where a native ear would catch it.
findings.direction: Use the 〜てん past, e.g. '埋めててん'. The same form occurs elsewhere in kansai_99_yn.js (言うてみたかったねん, 真似したねん) and in about six lines in other regions.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: あの一座は、私の家だった。十六で初めて台詞をもらって、コウメと二人で漫才をして。笑い声が、毎晩帰る場所だった。
findings.en: That troupe was my home. At sixteen I got my first lines, and Koume and I did our double act. The laughter was where I came home to, every night.
findings.kansai: あの一座は、私の家やった。十六で初めて台詞をもろて、コウメと二人で漫才をして。笑い声が、毎晩帰る場所やったねん。
findings.why: Kansai 帰る場所やったねん is the same 〜たねん error, here in a tender line. The line also keeps 私 where the Kansai track elsewhere uses うち.
findings.direction: e.g. '帰る場所やってん' (or 'やったんや').

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: 戻れば、全部戻ってくる。……それを、一晩だけ想像したかったの。断る前に、ちゃんと。
findings.en: If I went back, I'd have all of it again. …I wanted one night just to imagine it. Properly, before I say no.
findings.kansai: 戻ったら、全部戻ってくる。……それを、一晩だけ想像したかったねん。断る前に、ちゃんと。
findings.why: Kansai 想像したかったねん is the same 〜たねん error. The style sheet's own model for this shape is 言うてみたかってん.
findings.direction: e.g. '想像したかってん'.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: ……嘘。あの幟。あれは……私の一座よ。
findings.en: …No. That banner. That's… my troupe.
findings.kansai: ……嘘や。あの幟。あれは……私の一座や。
findings.why: The Kansai style sheet makes うち Suzu's 'I'. Across the game, 116 Kansai lines use うち and only five use 私, and all five are in kansai_99_yn.js: this line, rokubei_first#d704dd662e, suzu_evening#b3e0fdfed1, suzu_garden#5e7264db3a and suzu_books#ad7c87649d. In this same part the Hall Kansai lines use うち, so a player on the Kansai track hears her pronoun switch between scenes for no reason.
findings.direction: Bring the five yn Kansai lines in line with うち (e.g. 'あれは……うちの一座や'), or record a deliberate reason for 私 in Steamhollow.

findings.speaker: yn_okiyo
findings.text: お風呂の決まり、ご存じですか。階段の横に、額がございます。湯船の前に、必ずかけ湯をお願いいたしますね。
findings.en: Do you know the bath rules? There's a framed notice by the stairs. Please be sure to rinse before you get in.
findings.why: 湯船の前に first reads as a place ('in front of the tub'), and only then as 'before getting in'. Inn staff would say 湯船に入る前に or お湯に入る前に. Tatsuzō's line in the same puzzle says 入る前に流す.
findings.direction: e.g. '湯船に入る前に、必ずかけ湯を…'.

findings.speaker: mio
findings.text: 静か……。でも、怖い静かさじゃない。誰かが片付けて、出て行った部屋みたい。
findings.en: So quiet… But not a frightening quiet. Like a room someone tidied before they left.
findings.why: The usual spoken noun is 静けさ. 静かさ exists but reads like a learner's derivation, especially in the set frame 怖い静けさ. Mio has the same pattern twice outside this part (lq.kh_arrive, sg.cove_arrive).
findings.direction: Use 静けさ, unless the echo of 静か… is wanted deliberately.

findings.speaker: nao
findings.text: 住所ができたなら、俺が配達に来る日も来るな。
findings.en: If there are addresses now, one day I'll be delivering here.
findings.why: 配達に来る日も来る repeats 来る back to back and sounds clumsy when spoken.
findings.direction: Avoid the doubled verb, e.g. 'いつか俺が配達に来ることになるな'.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: 最終幕の舞台は、私たちの旅。演出、憎いわね。
findings.en: The last act is set on our own journey. Whoever staged this knows what they're doing.
findings.why: 憎い here is the admiring 'cleverly done' sense (as in 心憎い, 憎い演出). A learner's dictionary gives 'hateful', the opposite of what she means. The Kansai variant 演出、憎いなあ has the same issue.
findings.direction: Add a register note on 憎い (admiring: 'so clever it's almost annoying'). No text change.

findings.speaker: yn_okiyo
findings.text: 手拭いは、頭の上に。湯には入れないでくださいまし。皆さまの湯ですから。
findings.en: Your towel goes on your head. Never in the water, please. The water is everyone's.
findings.why: 〜くださいまし (also in okiyo_idle#6dfd507005, ご覧になってくださいましね) is old-fashioned service or shitamachi speech, and Okiyo is the only speaker who uses it. It is right for her as a character, but a learner may copy it as ordinary polite Japanese.
findings.direction: Add a register note: an old-fashioned, inn-maid flavoured 'please'; everyday polite speech is 〜ください. No text change.

findings.speaker: hall_karakasa
findings.addressee: nobody (failure branch of the umbrella encounter; the text is scene description)
findings.text: ……ぽつ、ぽつ。雨の音だけが、返事のように続いている。
findings.en: …Drip, drip. Only the rain answers, on and on.
findings.why: This is third-person narration (the umbrella does NOT answer; only the rain goes on), but the source has it as a hall_karakasa: line (24_w4_scenes.js:405), so the umbrella's actor would be recorded describing their own silence.
findings.direction: Make it a narr: line (not voiced), or give the umbrella a real spoken refusal; e.g. narr: 傘は答えない。雨の音だけが、返事のように続いている。

findings.speaker: hall_mame
findings.addressee: nobody (failure branch of the Mame encounter; the text is scene description)
findings.text: ……ぽん、ぽん。太鼓の音が、杉の奥で続いている。
findings.en: …Pon, pon. The drumming goes on, deep in the cedars.
findings.why: Same fault as the umbrella: narration of the drumming continuing (Mame has walked off) is assigned to hall_mame (23_w3_scenes.js:417), so Mame's actor would read a stage description aloud as dialogue.
findings.direction: Make it a narr: line; if Mame should be heard, only the ぽん、ぽん could be a sound effect.

findings.speaker: any (comp)
findings.addressee: pc (fellow traveller; said by whichever companion is present)
findings.text: 書いてある順じゃなくて、前と後で決まる順。上手くいったね。
findings.en: Not the order it was written in, but the order before and after make. Well done.
findings.why: No scene in this part branches by companion, so all 45 unique generic comp: lines (105 placements) are spoken by Ren too. None has a polite form: 21 end in plain ね/だね and about a dozen are plain volitionals (〜よう, 〜おうか？). Ren's own lines in the same tales are consistently です/ます (e.g. w3.f3_first 鐘は、時を告げるものです), and across the game Ren has 0 だね and 0 plain volitionals; Nao ends with ね in 12 of 1090 lines (な in 189). Ren would flip to casual ね-talk between their own polite lines, and Nao would sound softened.
findings.direction: Branch the payoff/hint lines per companion as the f1_first/t6/end scenes already do, or rewrite generic lines as register-neutral fragments (noun endings, no ね/よう/だ) that all four can say. The same applies to 5966a979dd, 92c9be23d2, 09004bf5fb, 8f86650978, 1483003e0e, 9b848b1311, 24ccbbdb22, 09daa2e39e, 2418206743, e95f731b64, d994c22be7, 3a13ff4c13, 2ef928e066, beb9d7b259, 5ef953afa3 and the もう一度言おうか？ family. e.g. '書いた順じゃなく、前と後の順。……揃った。'

findings.speaker: any (comp)
findings.text: 見た順番に並べたら、最後の場所にいるはずだ。
findings.en: Put the sightings in order, and the cub should be where it was seen last.
findings.why: A plain declarative ending in だ (also hall.w6.ibuki#3fbfa92a02 例外が多そうだ) is Nao's voice; Mio and Suzu normally soften it (はずよ/はずね) and Ren would say はずです, so as a generic line it fits one companion in four.
findings.direction: Drop the sentence-final copula or branch per companion; e.g. '見た順に並べれば、最後の場所に……。'

findings.speaker: mio
findings.text: 前に、後で、まで、までに。全部、間に合うための言葉だったのね。
findings.en: Before, after, until, by. They were all words for being in time.
findings.why: At every tale's end in this part, only Mio recites the lesson's grammar list: also w4.end#a4ebc72219 (頼む、許す、つもり), w5.end#85bfc4367c (から、のに、おかげ、せい) and w6.end#bfa1265e75 (なら、たら、ても、ただし). The other three companions react to the story, but Mio becomes the lesson-summary voice, so the teaching text leaks into her speech and casts her as the party's teacher.
findings.direction: Keep her reflective second sentence and move the list of forms to the recap UI, or let her mention one form naturally; e.g. '間に合うための言葉ばかりだったのね。'

findings.speaker: any (comp)
findings.text: 決まりの通り。「ても」と「ただし」を見落とさなくてよかった。
findings.en: All by the board. Good thing we didn't miss the "even if" and the "however".
findings.why: A companion congratulating the player on not missing the grammar items ても and ただし sounds like a teacher, not like someone at a toll gate. Similar: hall.w3.h_bridge#09004bf5fb 前に、後で、間に合った. By contrast, 2cd7f855ac quoting the board's literal ただし is fine, because the word is written on the board.
findings.direction: Refer to the people and the situation, not the grammar; e.g. '雨の人も、子供も、決まりの通りに通れた。'

findings.speaker: any (comp)
findings.text: しなければならないこと、してもいいこと、してはいけないこと。分けて覚えよう。
findings.en: What we must do, what we may do, what we mustn't. Let's keep them apart.
findings.why: It lists the three modal patterns in their textbook form and then says 'let's memorise them separately', which is a study tip. At a temple gate the only real need is to follow the three rules.
findings.direction: Make it about the rules in front of them; e.g. 'どれが決まりで、どれがしなくていいことか、よく見よう。'

findings.speaker: any (comp)
findings.text: 「赤いの」「さっきの」。名前を言わなくても、話の流れで分かるね。
findings.en: "The red one", "the one from before": no names needed, the conversation carries it.
findings.why: This is commentary on how the の-pronoun works, spoken as banter after fetching bowls. People don't remark on how reference works, so the lesson's explanation leaks into the companion's voice.
findings.direction: React to the result (the set is complete, Owan is pleased) and leave the grammar point to the lesson.

findings.speaker: hall_shino
findings.addressee: pc and companion (helpers met tonight; she uses です/ます with them)
findings.text: 祖父の石板の通りにできた。次は、上へ。
findings.en: All done as the slate says. Up we go.
findings.why: Shino speaks to the party in です/ます with the outsider-facing 祖父 (shino2, shino3, t6). Here she keeps 祖父 but switches to plain できた, a mix that fits neither her polite voice nor her private one (alone she says おじいちゃん, w3.end#2390e8162e).
findings.direction: Either keep it polite (e.g. '祖父の石板の通りにできました。次は、上です。') or make it clearly relieved self-talk with おじいちゃん.

findings.speaker: hall_shino
findings.text: 子供を探すなら、見た人に聞いてみましょう。一番最後に見たのは、誰か。
findings.en: If we're looking for a child, let's ask the people who saw them. Who saw them last.
findings.why: The final fragment 〜のは、誰か。 is written, headline-style Japanese, and spoken after a pause it is easily heard as 誰か, 'someone' ('the one who saw them last is someone').
findings.direction: Make the question form explicit in her polite register; e.g. '一番最後に見たのが誰か、ですね。'

findings.speaker: hall_gosaku
findings.addressee: pc (helper he otherwise addresses in です/ます)
findings.text: ミョウシンさまが、縁側にいらっしゃる。寺の決まりを守って、上がらせてもらおう。
findings.en: Myōshin is on the veranda. Let's keep the temple's rules and ask to go up.
findings.why: Gosaku is polite to the player in gosaku1, in the t6 reading offer (読みましょう…知りたいんですか) and at the end (来年の梅雨も…来ます). This face-the-player suggestion, between those lines, is plain volitional, and next to the honorific いらっしゃる it sounds half-polite. As a mutter to himself it works; as a suggestion to the player it jars.
findings.direction: If addressed to the player, make it polite; e.g. '上がらせてもらいましょう。' Otherwise tell the actor it is self-talk.

findings.speaker: hall_hanbei
findings.addressee: pc (stranger, acting for the toll-gate keeper)
findings.text: 「町の商人だ。荷物がたくさんある。」
findings.en: "I'm a merchant from the town, with a heavy load of cloth to sell."
findings.why: A merchant introducing himself in bare plain だ to whoever sets his toll sounds gruff, not brisk; x_hanbei#9590d126f9 (一人だ。提灯はない。) is the same. Ofuku (a medicine seller) also speaks plain わ/の to the same stranger, while the pilgrim Kōun is polite. Plain speech is not wrong for a brisk man, but at a checkpoint a native listener would expect at least です.
findings.direction: Keep him brisk but polite at the gate (e.g. '町の商人です。荷物が多くてね。'), or establish in the scene that he already knows the player.

findings.speaker: hall_mosuke
findings.text: 「腰を痛めたせいで、立っていられん。じゃが、座って数を数えるだけならできる。」
findings.en: "My back hurts, so I can't work standing. But leave the counting to me."
findings.why: Old-man folk-tale role language appears with no register note: copula じゃ, じゃが, じゃから, じゃろう and 〜ん negatives (立っていられん, 聞かん). Kihei uses the same forms: b34a9ebb37 玉に瑕じゃがな (frozen VA2), bacc45a5b9 and adbb8fe9db 変わらん…だけじゃ. The only general lexicon gloss for じゃ is 'casual form of では', which mis-explains 無理じゃ / 良い字じゃ. The voice suits both men and should stay.
findings.direction: No text change. Add a register note: じゃ = だ in older, folk-tale speech; 〜ん = 〜ない; recognise it, but do not copy it for your own speech.

findings.speaker: hall_osho
findings.text: 子狸を見たか、と？見たとも。
findings.en: Did I see a tanuki cub? I did.
findings.why: The echo question 〜か、と？ and the emphatic 〜とも ('certainly') are marked, older and warm forms that a beginner will not parse, and the scene gives no note. They suit the mild priest.
findings.direction: No text change. Note: 〜とも = 'of course, certainly' (older, kindly); 'Xか、と？' = 'you ask whether X?'

findings.speaker: any (comp)
findings.text: 暦の言葉、もう一度言おうか？
findings.en: Shall I say the almanac's words again?
findings.why: 'Xの言葉' for what a written document says is shaped by English ('the almanac's words'). The template recurs: 紙の言葉 (34bf3fb9a8), 高札の言葉 (7fdb40c50c), 記録の言葉 (883c46040f), 帳面の言葉 (f4c170140b). Speakers say 何て書いてあったか or simply offer to read it again.
findings.direction: e.g. '暦、もう一度読もうか？' (and resolve the generic-companion register at the same time).

findings.speaker: hall_osugi
findings.text: 直った！ありがとう。
findings.en: It's fixed! Thank you.
findings.why: The line is shared with the children Kōta and Hatsu. For Osugi, a tart and stubborn old neighbour (聞きたくないね / 昔は甘かったのさ), a bright, child-like exclamation flattens her voice.
findings.direction: Give Osugi her own short thanks in her ね/さ register; e.g. '水が来たね。……助かったよ。'

findings.speaker: nao
findings.text: 宛先のない手紙は届けない。ただし、困っている人の手紙は、何としてでも届ける。配達の決まりも、同じだ。
findings.en: No address, no delivery. Except a letter from someone in trouble: that gets there, whatever it takes. The delivery rules are the same.
findings.why: Nao closes four tales in this part with the same 'it's like delivery' moral: w3.end#b2ad726196 手紙と同じだ, w4.t1#9e1ac16b51 配達も、同じだ, w5.end#0795f97247 同じことだな, and this line. This one also restates the lesson's ただし rule in three full sentences, which reads like a fable's moral rather than the wry, short-sentenced courier.
findings.direction: Vary Nao's closers, keep them short and wry, and drop the explicit 同じだ equation.

findings.speaker: hall_mame
findings.addressee: pc and companion (the helpers who found her cub)
findings.text: 夜は終わった。でも、また来るね。……ありがとう。
findings.en: The night is over. But it'll come again, won't it. …Thank you.
findings.why: Without a subject, with ね and followed by ありがとう, また来るね is heard as Mame's own farewell ('I'll come again'), not 'night will come again' as the English intends. The actor will need to know which meaning to play.
findings.direction: If night is meant, make the subject explicit; e.g. 'でも、夜はまた来る。'

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: 手紙の言葉、もう一度言おうか？
findings.en: Shall I say what the letter said again?
findings.why: These scenes have no companion branch, so Ren records this line too. Ren's offer in the same world is polite (hall.w7.t6#8a40ba3559 「私が読みましょう。何を知りたいですか？」). A plain 言おうか？ from Ren a minute later is a jump a native listener would notice. The same line also plays in m_flute and m_mirror, and the same template appears in every Hall world (w1–w10).
findings.direction: Give Ren a polite variant or use one wording that suits all four companions. Fix the shared template in all worlds at once. e.g. (Ren) 「手紙の言葉、もう一度読みましょうか。」

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: 書き置きの言葉、もう一度言おうか？
findings.en: Shall I say what the note said again?
findings.why: This is the same offer template as in w7, with no companion branch, and it also plays in r_shrine and r_west. Ren's offer in this world is 「私が読みましょう。何を知りたいですか？」 (hall.w8.t6#8a40ba3559), so the plain version breaks Ren's voice.
findings.direction: Give Ren a polite variant or use one wording that suits all four companions.

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: 頼みの言葉、もう一度言おうか？
findings.en: Shall I say what she asked again?
findings.why: The gap is widest here. Ren's own line just before, in hall.w9.t6#34fb47bd94, is humble keigo (「何をお話ししましょうか。」), and then Ren would offer 「もう一度言おうか？」 in plain form. The line also plays in d_meal.
findings.direction: Give Ren a polite variant. e.g. (Ren) 「もう一度、お話ししましょうか。」

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: 名札を、合う足跡に置いていこう。
findings.en: Let's set each name tag by the prints that match.
findings.why: This is a plain volitional invitation to the player. In this part, every invitation Ren makes uses ましょう (一緒に行きましょう, 書き込みましょう, 貼りましょう, 見つけましょう). A plain 〜ていこう is out of voice for Ren.
findings.direction: Give Ren a polite variant or use one wording that suits all four companions. e.g. (Ren) 「名札を、合う足跡に置いていきましょう。」

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: 名札を、今夜の席に置いていこう。
findings.en: Let's set each name tag on tonight's seat.
findings.why: This is the same plain volitional invitation as hall.w8.t8_board#96e8ee23b1, and Ren would have to say it.
findings.direction: Give Ren a polite variant or use one wording that suits all four companions.

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: 何のことか書いてないのに、読めば分かる。書いた人も、分かると思って書いたんだね。
findings.en: None of them says what it means, and yet you can tell. Whoever wrote them trusted the reader to know.
findings.why: Every ANY(comp) puzzle-close line in w7–w9 is plain and ends in 〜(んだ)ね, aimed at the player. That fits Nao, Mio and Suzu. Ren does use plain fragments when musing, but never plain 〜んだね aimed at the player. This line stands for the set: 5ef953afa3, 4610cbe88b, be27b500f5, 3f6196cb8f, 4d57d0f1a2, 56f026b7a2, 8f7a712b76, 49dde6b30f, e1ac907d7a, 3001ba569c, 9c1181be39, f2a6aa727f, b556b748f3, e851ac516c, a2eab602b5, 90590e3802, 276c912f19, d488597780.
findings.direction: Either record Ren-specific polite variants of these closers, or drop the ね tags so the lines read as musing that suits all four. e.g. (Ren) 「…分かると思って書いたんですね。」

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: 「そうだ」も「らしい」も、人から聞いた話。でも、ヒサはそれを信じて歩いていったんだね。
findings.en: Whether it's そうだ or らしい, it's something Hisa heard. And Hisa trusted it, and walked.
findings.why: This is a grammar label recited in a companion's voice, and it is wrong for one pattern. The same line plays at r_west (pat=1), where Hisa's note uses みたい / らしい / 〜に違いない from her own inference about the teahouse lamp, not hearsay. That contradicts this world's own seen/heard/told/guessed lesson.
findings.direction: Drop the grammar labels and keep the emotional half, which works for both patterns. e.g. 「ヒサは、それを信じて歩いていったんだね。」

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: 「あれ」も「それ」も、相手が何を知っているかで決まるんだね。
findings.en: Are or sore: which one you say depends on what the other person knows.
findings.why: This is the teaching rule spoken by the companion as a recap, and it is the kind of teaching leak the spec asks to keep apart from character speech. hall.w7.b_rs#5ef953afa3 (「赤いの」「さっきの」。名前を言わなくても、話の流れで分かるね。) does the same.
findings.direction: Move the rule to the learning or feedback text, and let the companion react to the scene instead (what the snow covered, who the saying was for).

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: どれだけ確かかを言い間違えると、話が全部信用できなくなるからね。
findings.en: Get how sure you are wrong, and nobody can trust any of it.
findings.why: It opens with a からね justification that answers nothing anyone said. It sounds like a tutor explaining why the wrong answer was wrong, not like a reaction to ink fading off a scroll.
findings.direction: Make it a reaction, or keep the explanation in the feedback text. e.g. 「一つ間違えるだけで、全部怪しく聞こえるね。」

findings.speaker: any
findings.text: 同じ注文が、門では仰せ、店ではご注文、家では「欲しいそうだ」になった。言葉は、相手に合わせて着替えるんだね。
findings.en: The same order was a decree at the gate, a commission at the shop and "he wants" at home. Words change their clothes to suit the listener.
findings.why: The recap quotes words the player did not hear. Nobody says ご注文 at the shop (Gensuke says 欲しいそうです or 〜とのことです). The gate says ご命令 at F/E. At prof I, the home line is 欲しいとさ. A learner checking against the scene will not find these words.
findings.direction: Quote only forms that appear in every tier, or paraphrase without quotes and keep the 着替える image.

findings.speaker: mio
findings.text: らしい、そうだ、に違いない。言葉一つで、どのくらい確かかまで伝わるのね。
findings.en: Seems, I hear, must be. One word, and it carries how sure you are.
findings.why: Mio's world-close lines turn into grammar recaps. This one lists the target forms, hall.w8.t1#88244fb699 does the same (見た、聞こえた、らしい…), and hall.w9.end#c43b7c0d01 repeats the formula 言葉一つで…のね. Her w7 close ties the lesson to her patients and sounds like her (「患者さんの話も、同じよ。」).
findings.direction: Tie the point to Mio's own life (apothecary notes, what a patient says against what they show) instead of listing forms, and vary the closing formula.

findings.speaker: nao
findings.text: 泊めてください、じゃなくて、泊めていただけませんか。知らない家の戸を叩くときの言い方だ。
findings.en: Not "let me stay", but "might I stay". That's how you knock on a stranger's door.
findings.why: Nao, impatient with ceremony, gives a keigo contrast lesson. Also, F-tier players saw 『とめてください』 on the scroll, and the t4 board says 『泊めてください』 at F/E, so Nao 'corrects' a form the scroll never showed them.
findings.direction: Keep the courier angle but make it a reaction, not a contrast drill. Make sure it does not contradict the kana-tier text. e.g. 「知らない家の戸を叩く時は、ああいう頼み方になる。配達でもそうだ。」

findings.speaker: hall_otoku
findings.addressee: pc (visitor who settled the quarrel), after the scene
findings.text: 頼むのと命じるのは、違うものですね。
findings.en: Asking and ordering are not the same thing, are they.
findings.why: With the visitor, Otoku is otherwise plain old-wife speech (〜んだよ, 置いておくれ, 何が知りたいんだい, 届いてこそだね). Here she switches to です/ね. Her polite 何を言うんですか / 聞きましょう toward her husband is folk-tale convention. But this world teaches 'plain for family, polite for guests', and Otoku inverts it in both directions with no note.
findings.direction: Make this 'after' line match her plain register to the visitor (e.g. 「頼むのと命じるのは、違うもんだね。」), or add a short register note on the old wife's polite speech to her husband.

findings.speaker: hall_omatsu
findings.text: ヒサの字です。一緒に読んでください。何が知りたいですか？
findings.en: It's Hisa's writing. Read it with me. What would you like to know?
findings.why: A careful innkeeper asking a guest 〜たいですか directly about their wishes sounds blunt (a known keigo pitfall), next to her otherwise courteous speech. A scene earlier she also said she can no longer read small writing.
findings.direction: Have her offer instead of asking about the guest's wishes. e.g. 「どこから読みましょうか。」

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: 見ていただけのところ。……客席からの場面ね。演じなくていい。それで十分。
findings.en: The part where you only watched. …A scene from the audience's side. No acting needed. That's plenty.
findings.why: 見ていただけ parses as 見て＋いただけ (humble いただく) as easily as 見ていた＋だけ. A learner or the word help may read keigo where there is none. Suzu elsewhere says 見てる / 見てた, and the Kansai line already has 見てただけ.
findings.direction: Use Suzu's own contraction. e.g. 「見てただけのところ。」

findings.speaker: nao
findings.text: 勝手に入ってきた口だな。人のことは言えないが。
findings.en: He's let himself in. Not that we can talk.
findings.why: The line is good, wry Nao, but 口 here means 'sort/type (of person)' (as in その口か). A learner glossing 口 as 'mouth' will be lost.
findings.direction: No text change. Give 口 the 'kind, type' sense in word help or a note.

findings.speaker: hall_gonroku
findings.text: 狐じゃ。昔から、物が消えれば狐と決まっておる。
findings.en: A fox. Since time out of mind, when a thing goes missing, it's a fox.
findings.why: じゃ / 〜ておる / わし / 見てもおらん are deliberate old-man role language for the rumour-monger. They are not stereotyping: Yosaku and Kichibei, also old men, speak plain without them. A learner still needs a note that this is storybook old-man speech, not a model.
findings.direction: No text change. Add a register note ('storybook old-man speech; everyday equivalent だ / いる').

findings.speaker: hall_envoy
findings.text: その言葉は、拙者に向けたものではあるまい。
findings.en: Those words were surely not meant for me.
findings.why: The samurai register (拙者, 参った, 〜まい, うむ, 下がれ) is right for the lord's haughty messenger in a tale. But 〜あるまい is literary negative conjecture, and learners know 参った mainly as 'I give up'.
findings.direction: No text change. Add a register note marking it as period samurai speech, with あるまい ≈ ないだろう.

findings.speaker: hall_otoku
findings.text: 囲炉裏の席は、誰がどこに座るか決まっているんだよ。板に書いてあるから、名札を置いておくれ。
findings.en: Everyone has their own place round the hearth. It's written on the board; would you set out the name tags?
findings.why: おくれ (and her later 何が知りたいんだい) is elder request/question speech that fits a folk-tale old wife. A learner will meet it here with no note and may copy it.
findings.direction: No text change. Add a note that おくれ is an old-fashioned, elderly form of 〜てくれ / 〜てください.

findings.speaker: hall_sabu
findings.text: おいら、じいちゃんの話、全部覚えているよ。
findings.en: I remember everything Grandad says.
findings.why: おいら is a rustic, storybook first-person pronoun for a village child. It fits the tale, but it is marked, and learners need to know it is not a neutral 'I'.
findings.direction: No text change. Add a register note on おいら.

findings.speaker: nao
findings.addressee: pc and Tsuru (close travelling companion; Tsuru a familiar elder), light banter
findings.text: 届け損ねた名前か。私の仕事だな。
findings.en: Undelivered names. Sounds like my line of work.
findings.why: This is the only 私 Nao says in the whole game (俺 x65 elsewhere, including in this same part: 俺とは気が合わないな, 俺の同業者だな). In a smirking aside, plain だな and 私 do not go together for Nao, and the change of pronoun reads as a slip, not as a choice.
findings.direction: Use Nao's usual pronoun, or leave the pronoun out. e.g. 「俺の仕事だな。」

findings.speaker: any (comp)
findings.addressee: pc (close companion) when choosing to head home from camp
findings.text: 引き返すのも、旅のうちだよ。
findings.en: Turning back is part of travelling too.
findings.why: Checked the source (src/atlas/60_scenes.js :home): this is a true ?(comp) line with no companion branch. Ren never uses 〜だよ/〜だね to the player anywhere in the game; the Ren voice would record a register the character never has. It fits Nao, Mio and Suzu (Kansai Suzu has its own override in kansai_90_atlas.js).
findings.direction: Split by companion with a polite Ren variant, or write a neutral fragment that suits all four. e.g. Ren: 「引き返すのも、旅のうちです。」

findings.speaker: any (comp)
findings.addressee: pc (close companion) after an early return
findings.text: 引き返す勇気も、大事だよ。
findings.en: It takes nerve to turn back, too.
findings.why: A true ?(var.atlas_kind=2&comp) line. The kind=1 and kind=3 outcomes right next to it are split per companion (Ren's are polite: 灯は消えていません。私たちもです。), but this one gives Ren plain だよ.
findings.direction: Split per companion, as the other two outcomes are. e.g. Ren: 「引き返す勇気も、大事です。」

findings.speaker: any (comp)
findings.addressee: pc (close companion), noticing a new path
findings.text: 森が、育ったんだね。
findings.en: The grove has grown.
findings.why: A true ?(comp) line (src/content/returns/10_kotonoha.js). 〜んだね fits Nao, Mio and Suzu but not Ren, who is polite to the player throughout this part.
findings.direction: Give Ren its own polite line, or use a neutral fragment for everyone. e.g. Ren: 「森が、育ったんですね。」

findings.speaker: any (comp)
findings.addressee: pc (close companion), reading the observatory rota
findings.text: 一人で待つ灯じゃなくなったんだね。
findings.en: It isn't a lamp that waits alone any more.
findings.why: A true ?(comp) line (src/content/returns/30_towns.js). The plain 〜じゃなくなったんだね cannot be said by Ren as written.
findings.direction: Add a Ren variant. e.g. 「一人で待つ灯では、なくなったんですね。」

findings.speaker: any (comp)
findings.addressee: pc (close companion), at the new ferry sign
findings.text: 前の看板は、字が消えていたよね。
findings.en: The old sign had lost its letters, hadn't it?
findings.why: A true ?(comp) line (src/content/zz_atlas_decor.js). 〜よね does not suit Ren. The uncontracted 消えていたよね is also slightly bookish for casual Nao or Suzu (消えてたよね/な is the spoken form).
findings.direction: Split by companion, or use a neutral line. e.g. Ren: 「前の看板は、字が消えていましたね。」

findings.speaker: any (comp)
findings.addressee: pc (close companion), at a new lantern
findings.text: 去年は、なかった村だね。
findings.en: That village wasn't there last year.
findings.why: A true ?(comp) line. Plain だね does not suit Ren.
findings.direction: Ren variant. e.g. 「去年は、なかった村ですね。」

findings.speaker: any (comp)
findings.text: 雪が降っても、これなら迷わないね。
findings.en: Even in snow, nobody will get lost now.
findings.why: A true ?(comp) line. Plain 〜ないね does not suit Ren. It is also a missed Ren joke, since Ren is the one who always gets lost.
findings.direction: Ren variant. e.g. 「これなら、私でも迷いません。……たぶん。」

findings.speaker: any (comp)
findings.addressee: pc (close companion), at the crate of returned tags
findings.text: 字が戻ると、荷物も帰れるんだね。
findings.en: When the letters come back, the cargo can go home too.
findings.why: A true ?(comp) line. 〜んだね does not suit Ren.
findings.direction: Ren variant. e.g. 「字が戻ると、荷物も帰れるんですね。」

findings.speaker: any (comp)
findings.addressee: pc (close companion), thinking aloud at a grate
findings.text: 向こう側からなら、開けられるかも。
findings.en: Maybe from the other side.
findings.why: A true ?(comp) line. A clipped かも, thought aloud, is a lighter mismatch than だよ (Ren does think aloud with 木の間かな), but elsewhere Ren always says 〜かもしれません. Every other companion line in this expedition is split per companion.
findings.direction: Optionally give Ren its own line. e.g. 「向こう側からなら、開けられるかもしれません。」

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.addressee: the troupe as audience (manzai bit on stage)
findings.text: この前、湯ノ谷で、毎晩温泉に入りました。……服を着たまま。
findings.en: The other day in Steamhollow, I got into the hot spring every night. …With my clothes on.
findings.kansai: この前、湯ノ谷で、毎晩温泉に入ったねん。……服を着たまま。
findings.why: The KANSAI version's 入ったねん is not native Osaka grammar: past + ねん contracts to 〜てん (入ってん). A Kansai listener hears 〜たねん as a non-native error. It also drops the stage politeness of the standard line (see rt.troupe#1b606941de). The same 〜たねん / 〜かったねん / 〜やったねん pattern occurs in the Kansai layer outside this part: ko.suzu_leaf#0ec2d52533, kr.makeup#fc506a8eae, mp.manzai#9f40be19f7, mp.rehearsal#51ee79e0f0, yn.bath_beat#19abc2bc96, yn.bath_scene#7abb670147, yn.suzu_books#ad7c87649d, yn.suzu_garden#5e7264db3a, yn.suzu_garden#c84867af1f.
findings.direction: Use 〜てん (or 〜たんや) throughout the Kansai layer. e.g. 「毎晩温泉に入ってん。」. If the bit stays stage-polite, 「入りました」 can stay as it is.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.addressee: the troupe as audience (manzai bit on stage)
findings.text: 昨日はね、雨が降ってきたから、口を開けて、上を向いていました。甘いのが降ると思って。
findings.en: Yesterday the rain came, so I stood with my mouth open, looking up. I thought something sweet would fall.
findings.kansai: 昨日はな、雨が降ってきたから、口を開けて、上を向いてたねん。甘いのが降ると思って。
findings.why: In the KANSAI version, 向いてたねん is the same non-native past + ねん error. Native Osaka says 向いててん. It is the punchline of the bit, so a wrong ending is especially audible.
findings.direction: e.g. 「口開けて、上向いててん。」

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: はい、どうもどうも！わたし、帳簿は完璧です。毎月、ぴったりゼロ。……財布もゼロ。
findings.en: Hello, hello! My books are perfect. Every month, exactly zero. …So's my purse.
findings.kansai: はい、どうもどうも！うち、帳簿は完璧やで。毎月、ぴったりゼロ。……財布もゼロ。
findings.why: The standard bit is delivered stage-polite (完璧です / 入りました / 向いていました), while the KANSAI bit turns every line plain (完璧やで / 入ったねん / 向いてたねん). docs/dialect/suzu_kansai.md says polite stage announcements stay polite. Plain manzai is a real Kansai convention, so this is a judgement call, but at present the dialect choice also changes the politeness.
findings.direction: Decide once: either keep the です/ました stage frame in Kansai and carry the dialect in particles and intonation, or treat the routine as plain manzai in both versions. e.g. Kansai: 「うち、帳簿は完璧です。」

findings.speaker: mio
findings.addressee: pc (committed travelling companion; can be late game or postgame, with no bond condition)
findings.text: さっきのしりとり、どうでしたか。私、途中で薬のことを一度も考えていないと気づきました。
findings.en: How was that game for you? Partway through, I noticed I hadn't thought about medicine once.
findings.why: The whole reflection is full です/ます (also 56f81291d8, 0fd391b3b9, 5b3f2077c4, 82240c8366, 5ee3c5ffd3, afa33af4e1, and even はい。また今度。). In the same companion stage in this part, Mio is soft plain to the player (お茶、淹れるね / 行こうか / 包帯とお茶、持った。行こう。). The scene is offered whenever she is the companion (available: s.comp), so a close, postgame Mio suddenly sounds like she is meeting a stranger. The shiritori lines in wordplay/10_lines.js are polite in the same way, so this is a module-level decision.
