findings.direction: Bring the module to Mio's companion register (soft plain with occasional ましょう), or gate a polite version to early bond only. e.g. 「さっきのしりとり、どうだった？」

findings.speaker: yasu
findings.text: ……川のこと、前に話したな。俺は何と言った？
findings.en: …I told you something about the river once. What did I say?
findings.why: This is Yasu's only 俺 in the game. Everywhere else he says わし (lq.road_yasu1, lq.road_write, lq.road_yasu2). The switch is unmotivated, and the same actor will voice both.
findings.direction: Use わし, or drop the pronoun. e.g. 「わしは何と言った？」 / 「何と言ったかな？」

findings.speaker: co_asa
findings.text: 屋台で、言葉の遊びができるのよ。八百橋から来た人が、教えてくれたの。
findings.en: There are word games at the stalls. Someone from Manybridge showed us how.
findings.why: Asa (teen, androgynous, youthful casual) never uses the mature-feminine 〜のよ in its other 15 lines: it says 〜んだもん, 〜よね, 〜だよ, 〜んだね. のよ makes Asa sound older and more gendered than written.
findings.direction: Keep Asa's own endings. e.g. 「言葉の遊びができるんだよ。」

findings.speaker: cr_ujie
findings.addressee: pc (traveller he once processed at the barrier), now at Gonza's teahouse
findings.text: 笑い話のつもりでしたが、本当に茶屋になりました。ゴンザのお茶は、関所の頃よりうまい。
findings.en: I meant it as a joke, but it really has become a teahouse. Gonza's tea is better than it ever was in the barrier days.
findings.why: Ujie is 'formal to the last syllable' (でございます, おります in every other line, including cr.ujie_after). Here he ends on a bare plain うまい, which is also a blunt word for taste. If it is a deliberate crack in his formality, it works, but it should be a decision.
findings.direction: Either keep it as a marked moment and note it for the actor, or keep his register. e.g. 「関所の頃より、うまいのです。」

findings.speaker: koji
findings.addressee: pc (a Reedwake local he knows well)
findings.text: 本日は増水の恐れがあるため、最終便の出航を見合わせる可能性がございます。
findings.en: With the river likely to rise today, the last boat may not sail.
findings.why: The ask-back exercise needs a hard, formal first version, and the simpler rephrasings are casual. But Kōji is everywhere else the PC's easygoing neighbour (よう、姉さん / 言うなよ), and the narration frames this as him 'explaining', not announcing. ございます / お勧めします (#e3d58dde3b) from him to a friend sounds like a different person.
findings.direction: Frame it as a public announcement (narration: Kōji reads the posted notice to the waiting passengers), or give the formal version to a generic ferry clerk.

findings.speaker: ren
findings.addressee: pc (companion), facing a bell that impersonates another's voice
findings.text: 灯落の鐘の音ではありません。私は知っています。
findings.en: That is not the voice of Lanternfall's bell. I know it.
findings.why: 「私は知っています」 standing alone after the denial reads like 'I know it.' rendered word for word. It is unclear what Ren knows (the real sound), and contrastive 私は sounds like a claim against someone.
findings.direction: Make the object explicit and keep Ren's calm. e.g. 「本物の音を、私は知っています。」

findings.speaker: ren
findings.addressee: pc (companion), reading a notice; a [teach te_aru] card follows immediately
findings.text: 「〜てあります」は、誰かが済ませて残した形です。灯りの帳面でもよく見ます。
findings.en: "〜て あります" is the shape of something someone finished and left. You see it in lamp logs all the time.
findings.why: Unlike the other three companions, who interpret the notice in their own words, Ren gives a grammar definition ('〜てあります is a form…') that duplicates the teach card right after it. The 〜 inside 「」 also has no spoken reading.
findings.direction: Let Ren read the notice in-world as the others do, and leave the terminology to the teach card. e.g. 「上げてあります……誰かが済ませて、置いていった。灯りの帳面と同じ書き方です。」

findings.speaker: co_goro
findings.text: 年寄りの話は、長くて覚えきれんからの。
findings.en: An old man's stories go on too long to keep.
findings.why: The elderly sentence-final の (からの, 言ったかの？ #29db4f10e7) together with 〜ておる / じゃ is old-man role speech. A learner will read の as a nominaliser or a question. The speech is fine for Goro, as profiled, but it needs a register note.
findings.direction: Add a register note on Goro's sentence-final の / 〜ておる / じゃ (elderly, regional-flavoured; compare 〜からね, 〜かね). No text change.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: 次の幕は議会堂ね。古い台本を読んでもらいましょう。
findings.en: Next act: the Council Chamber. Let's have someone read the old script aloud.
findings.kansai: 次の幕は議会堂やな。古い台本を読んでもらお。
findings.why: The standard line has polite forms (ましょう); the Kansai version drops them, so choosing Kansai also makes her less polite here.
findings.direction: Keep the politeness of the standard line in the Kansai version (Kansai has polite forms too: 〜ます, 〜まひょ / 〜ましょか, 〜はる), or make both versions plain if the standard one should be.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: 貸し借りは、きっちり返してもらいましょう。町一つ分の「いいえ」、利子をつけてね。
findings.en: Let's make sure the debts get settled properly. One whole town's worth of "no"s — with interest.
findings.kansai: 貸し借りは、きっちり返してもらお。町一つ分の「いいえ」、利子つけてな。
findings.why: The standard line has polite forms (ましょう); the Kansai version drops them, so choosing Kansai also makes her less polite here.
findings.direction: Keep the politeness of the standard line in the Kansai version (Kansai has polite forms too: 〜ます, 〜まひょ / 〜ましょか, 〜はる), or make both versions plain if the standard one should be.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: 役の名前を忘れた役者は、舞台に立てないのよ。思い出させてあげましょう。
findings.en: An actor who's forgotten their part's name can't go on. Let's help it remember.
findings.kansai: 役の名前忘れた役者は、舞台に立たれへんねん。思い出さしてあげよ。
findings.why: The standard line has polite forms (ましょう); the Kansai version drops them, so choosing Kansai also makes her less polite here.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: 六十年の幕間ね。次の幕、始めましょう。

findings.kansai: 六十年の幕間やな。次の幕、始めよか。

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: ……笑って済む話じゃなくなったわね。一番の橋、名前を返してもらいましょう。

findings.kansai: ……笑って済む話やなくなったな。一番の橋、名前返してもらお。

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: 昨日はね、箸を渡って、橋でご飯を食べました。
findings.en: Yesterday I crossed the chopsticks and ate my rice with a bridge.
findings.kansai: 昨日はな、箸を渡って、橋でご飯食べたねん。

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: この前、湯ノ谷で、毎晩温泉に入りました。……服を着たまま。
findings.en: The other day in Steamhollow, I got into the hot spring every night. …With my clothes on.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: 昨日はね、雨が降ってきたから、口を開けて、上を向いていました。甘いのが降ると思って。
findings.en: Yesterday the rain came, so I stood with my mouth open, looking up. I thought something sweet would fall.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: また幕を開けましょう。次の舞台も楽しみにしてるわ。
findings.en: Let's raise the curtain again. I'm looking forward to the next show.
findings.kansai: また幕開けよな。次の舞台も楽しみにしてるわ。
findings.why: The standard line has polite forms (ましょう); the Kansai version drops them, so choosing Kansai also makes her less polite here.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: 一つ百文で売れるわよ、これ。……冗談よ。配りましょう。
findings.en: These would sell for a hundred mon apiece. …Joking. Let's hand them out.
findings.kansai: 一つ百文で売れるで、これ。……冗談や。配ろ。
findings.why: The standard line has polite forms (ましょう); the Kansai version drops them, so choosing Kansai also makes her less polite here.

findings.speaker: nao
findings.text: ……入口から来たなら、足元気をつけて。三つ目の床板、抜けてるから。
findings.en: …If you came in the front, watch your step. The third floorboard is gone.
findings.why: The spoken text drops the learner spacing, so 元気 (meant あしもと+き) can be read as げんき. A voice may take 足元 + 元気 and say あしもとげんき.
findings.direction: Give the recording text the game's reading at this seam (kana, or a pause mark), or reword so the words do not join.

findings.speaker: suzu
findings.text: 返済計画を立てよう。利子も含めて。帳簿はわたしが付ける。毎月見に来るからね。誤魔化したら、すぐ分かるよ。
findings.en: We'll draw up a repayment plan. Interest included. I'll keep the books, and I'll check them every month. Fiddle them and I'll know at once.
findings.why: The spoken text drops the learner spacing, so 月見 (meant まいつき+み) can be read as つきみ. 毎月見に can be taken as 毎 + 月見 (moon-viewing).
findings.direction: Give the recording text the game's reading at this seam (kana, or a pause mark), or reword so the words do not join.

findings.speaker: ren
findings.text: 書架の列を二回数えました。答えが違いました。
findings.en: I've counted the aisles in the Stacks twice. I got two different answers.
findings.why: The spoken text drops the learner spacing, so 回数 (meant にかい+かぞ) can be read as かいすう. 二回数えました is a known trap for voices: 回数 (かいすう).
findings.direction: Give the recording text the game's reading at this seam (kana, or a pause mark), or reword so the words do not join.

findings.speaker: ren
findings.text: 四百十二。同じ星を二回数えた可能性は、否定できません。

findings.why: The spoken text drops the learner spacing, so 回数 (meant にかい+かぞ) can be read as かいすう. 二回数えた: 回数 (かいすう) trap.
findings.direction: Give the recording text the game's reading at this seam (kana, or a pause mark), or reword so the words do not join.

findings.speaker: mio
findings.text: 誰が誰に、何を。全部分かると、優しい話だったのね。

findings.why: The spoken text drops the learner spacing, so 部分 (meant ぜんぶ+わ) can be read as ぶぶん. 全部分かると is a known trap for voices: 部分 (ぶぶん).

findings.text: あれ、合わないね。後でもう一回数えよう。

shared.text: 前の看板は、字が消えていたよね。
shared.en: The old sign had lost its letters, hadn't it?

shared.text: 去年は、なかった村だね。
shared.en: That village wasn't there last year.

shared.text: 雪が降っても、これなら迷わないね。
shared.en: Even in snow, nobody will get lost now.

shared.text: 字が戻ると、荷物も帰れるんだね。
shared.en: When the letters come back, the cargo can go home too.

shared.text: 引き返すのも、旅のうちだよ。
shared.en: Turning back is part of travelling too.

shared.text: 引き返す勇気も、大事だよ。
shared.en: It takes nerve to turn back, too.

shared.text: 絵も、やっと帰ってきたね。
shared.en: The picture's finally come home.

shared.text: 灯が全部点いたら、ほどけるんだろう。
shared.en: I expect it unties once all the lights are lit.

shared.text: 札がある。先に読んでから、歩こう。
shared.en: There's a card. Let's read it before we walk.

shared.text: 角を数え直してみようか。入り口から、もう一度。
shared.en: Shall we count the corners again? From the way in, once more.

shared.text: 順番が違ったみたいだ。札をもう一度読もう。
shared.en: Wrong order, it seems. Let's read the note again.

shared.text: 道しるべがすぐそこにある。見てから答えてもいいね。
shared.en: The signpost is right there. We could look before we answer.

shared.text: 正しい三つがあるから、違う一つが分かるんだね。
shared.en: It's because three are right that the odd one shows.

shared.text: 角を数えながら行こう。
shared.en: Let's count the corners as we go.

shared.text: 地図の言葉、もう一度言おうか？
shared.en: Shall I say what the map said again?

shared.text: 地図の通りだ。読んで、歩いて、見つけた。
shared.en: Just as the map said. Read it, walked it, found it.

shared.text: 九つの灯、全部見覚えがあるね。
shared.en: All nine lights look familiar.

shared.text: 書き付けの言葉、もう一度言おうか？
shared.en: Shall I say what the note said again?

shared.text: 止めた人たちが、続きを待っていたんだね。
shared.en: The ones who stopped were waiting for someone to go on.

shared.text: 自分の旅を、自分の言葉で書く。……最初の頃は、考えられなかったね。
shared.en: Writing your own journey in your own words. …Back at the start, you couldn't have imagined it.

shared.text: 一つ一つは寄り道みたいだったけど、並べるとちゃんと道になっているね。
shared.en: Each one felt like a detour at the time, but laid out together they make a road.

shared.text: 札を、通った順に道標へ置いていこう。
shared.en: Let's set the tablets on the waystones in the order we passed through.

shared.text: 全部、どこかで一度習ったことだ。忘れてないものだね。
shared.en: Every one of them something we learned somewhere along the way. We haven't forgotten.

shared.text: 道を聞くのも、断るのも、人の話を伝えるのも、全部この館で練習したんだね。
shared.en: Asking the way, saying no, passing on what someone said: we practised all of it in this Hall.

shared.text: 並び順が分からなくて、困っているみたいだ。
shared.en: They seem stuck: nobody knows the order to walk in.

shared.text: 札をもう一度読もう。誰の後ろに誰、か。
shared.en: Let's read the card again. Who walks behind whom.

shared.text: 仲人は、誰が誰に、を間違えたら仕事にならないからね。
shared.en: A go-between who mixes up who gives to whom is out of work.

shared.text: 先頭から順番に、声をかけていこう。
shared.en: Let's call them out in order, from the front.

shared.text: 紙の言葉、もう一度言おうか？
shared.en: Shall I say what the list said again?

shared.text: 傘を貸した人が、一番いい席に座る。正しい並びだね。
shared.en: The one who lent the umbrella sits in the best seat. The right arrangement.

shared.text: 貸した人に返す。借りた人じゃないよ。
shared.en: Back to whoever lent it. Not whoever borrowed it.

shared.text: 誰から、誰へ。札の字一つで、行き先が変わるんだね。
shared.en: From whom, to whom. One word on a tag, and the gift goes somewhere else.

shared.text: 書いてある順じゃなくて、前と後で決まる順。上手くいったね。
shared.en: Not the order it was written in, but the order before and after make. Well done.

shared.text: 一緒に登ろう。順番に、一つずつ。
shared.en: We'll climb with you. In order, one thing at a time.

shared.text: 急がなくていい。線香は、まだある。
shared.en: No need to hurry. There's more incense.

shared.text: 前に、後で、間に合った。時計と仲良くなった気分だね。
shared.en: Before, after, in time. I feel like the clock and I are friends now.

shared.text: 一番最後に見たのは、誰だった？
shared.en: Who saw it last?

shared.text: 大丈夫。お母さんのところへ帰ろう。
shared.en: It's all right. Let's get you back to your mother.

shared.text: 書いてある順と、やる順は、違うかもしれない。前と後をよく見よう。
shared.en: The order it's written in may not be the order to do it in. Watch for before and after.

shared.text: 鐘撞きは、前と後を間違えたら仕事にならないからね。
shared.en: A bell-ringer who mixes up before and after is out of a job.

shared.text: 暦の言葉、もう一度言おうか？
shared.en: Shall I say the almanac's words again?

shared.text: これで、村の人も鐘の時が分かる。
shared.en: Now the village will know the bell's hour too.

shared.text: 見た順番に並べたら、最後の場所にいるはずだ。
shared.en: Put the sightings in order, and the cub should be where it was seen last.

shared.text: 一年前、ゴサクさんはここで足止めされたんだね。
shared.en: A year ago, this is where Gosaku was stopped.

shared.text: 行くつもりの道と、本当に行った道。一年前のゴサクさんに、追い付いたね。
shared.en: The way he meant and the way he went. We've caught up with Gosaku as he was a year ago.

shared.text: 何を頼んでいたか、もう一度聞いてみよう。
shared.en: Let's hear again what they were asking for.

shared.text: はっきり言わない頼みも、聞けば分かるものだね。
shared.en: Even a request nobody says outright makes sense once you listen.

shared.text: 全部、決まりの通り。これなら、誰にも叱られないね。
shared.en: All by the rules. Nobody can scold us now.

shared.text: 頼み方を間違えたら、商売にならないからね。
shared.en: Ask the wrong way and there's no trade at all.

shared.text: 行くつもりだった道じゃなくて、本当に行った道を辿ろう。
shared.en: Not the way he meant to go: the way he really went.

shared.text: しなければならないこと、してもいいこと、してはいけないこと。分けて覚えよう。
shared.en: What we must do, what we may do, what we mustn't. Let's keep them apart.

shared.text: 高札の言葉、もう一度言おうか？
shared.en: Shall I say the notice's words again?

shared.text: 渡ってもいい所から、渡る。一年前のゴサクさんも、そうしたかっただろうね。
shared.en: We cross where crossing is allowed. Gosaku would have wanted to, a year ago.

shared.text: 桶を叩いても、桶は上がらないもんね。
shared.en: Banging the bucket would never have brought it up.

shared.text: ここには、困ったことが見えているだけ。どうしてそうなったか、誰かに聞いてみよう。
shared.en: Here the trouble only shows. Let's ask someone why it happens.

shared.text: 苦い井戸、か。誰のせいかより、何が理由かを知りたいね。
shared.en: The bitter well. Never mind whose fault; I'd like to know what the reason is.

shared.text: できない理由を聞けば、できることも分かる。上手く分けられたね。
shared.en: Hear why someone can't, and you learn what they can. Nicely shared out.

shared.text: 記録の言葉、もう一度言おうか？
shared.en: Shall I say what the record said again?

shared.text: 理由が分かれば、直し方も分かる。誰のせいでもなかったね。
shared.en: Know the reason and you know the remedy. It was nobody's fault after all.

shared.text: 理由が合わないと、話が全部おかしくなるからね。
shared.en: When the reason doesn't fit, the whole story goes wrong.

shared.text: 誰に何ができるか、理由を聞いてから決めよう。
shared.en: Let's hear everyone's reasons before we decide who does what.

shared.text: 東だから甘い、西だから苦い、じゃないんだね。理由を最後まで読まないと。
shared.en: It's not "east, so sweet" and "west, so bitter". You have to read the reason to the end.

shared.text: 暗くなる前に、灯籠を灯さないと。でも、決まりがあるみたいだね。
shared.en: We should light the lanterns before it's dark. But there seems to be a rule.

shared.text: 雨なら傘、暗くなったら提灯。決まりというより、親切の一覧だね。
shared.en: An umbrella if it rains, a lantern once it's dark. Less a list of rules than a list of kindnesses.

shared.text: 札の決まり、先に読もう。例外が多そうだ。
shared.en: Let's read the board first. Looks like lots of exceptions.

shared.text: 「全部灯す」でも、「ただし」が一つ。例外を見落とさなくてよかった。
shared.en: "Light them all", with one "however". Good thing we didn't miss the exception.

shared.text: 決まりの通り。「ても」と「ただし」を見落とさなくてよかった。
shared.en: All by the board. Good thing we didn't miss the "even if" and the "however".

shared.text: ……イブキと話そう。
shared.en: …Let's talk to Ibuki.

shared.text: 条件が合わないと、言葉が全部逆さまになるからね。
shared.en: When the condition doesn't fit, the whole saying comes out backwards.

shared.text: どの場合に、何をするのか。合う組み合わせを探そう。
shared.en: Which case calls for what. Let's find what goes together.

shared.text: 帳面の言葉、もう一度言おうか？
shared.en: Shall I say what the ledger said again?

shared.text: 夜は通さない。ただし、一つだけ例外がある。読んでよかったね。
shared.en: Nobody after dark, except in one case. Good thing we read it.

shared.text: 「赤いの」「さっきの」。名前を言わなくても、話の流れで分かるね。
shared.en: "The red one", "the one from before": no names needed, the conversation carries it.

shared.text: 何を、とは一言も書いてないのに、台所に立つと分かる。毎日のことだからだね。
shared.en: It never once says what, and yet standing in the kitchen you know. Because it's the same every day.

shared.text: ……誰もいないのに、誰かの話し声が聞こえるような気がする。
shared.en: …There's nobody here, but it feels as if I can hear someone talking.

shared.text: 何のことか書いてないのに、読めば分かる。書いた人も、分かると思って書いたんだね。
shared.en: None of them says what it means, and yet you can tell. Whoever wrote them trusted the reader to know.

shared.text: 手紙の言葉、もう一度言おうか？
shared.en: Shall I say what the letter said again?

shared.text: 名前を書かなくても、家族には分かったんだね。分かる人に向けて書いた手紙だ。
shared.en: Even without naming it, the family would have known. It was written for someone who would understand.

shared.text: 札には、何のことか、書いてないね。読めば分かるのかな。
shared.en: The notes don't say what they mean. I suppose you can tell by reading them.

shared.text: 「あれ」も「それ」も、相手が何を知っているかで決まるんだね。
shared.en: Are or sore: which one you say depends on what the other person knows.

shared.text: 証人が立っていた場所に行けば、本当に見えたか、聞こえたか、確かめられるね。
shared.en: If we go to where each witness was, we can check whether they really could have seen or heard it.

shared.text: 本人が確かだと思っていても、場所を見ると違うこともある。嘘じゃなくて、思い込みだね。
shared.en: Even when someone is sure, the place itself can show otherwise. Not a lie: a mistaken belief.

shared.text: 見た話、聞こえた話、聞いた話。全部合わせると、雪の上で一つになったね。
shared.en: What was seen, heard and told: put together, it all comes to one thing in the snow.

shared.text: 書き置きの言葉、もう一度言おうか？
shared.en: Shall I say what the note said again?

shared.text: 「そうだ」も「らしい」も、人から聞いた話。でも、ヒサはそれを信じて歩いていったんだね。
shared.en: Whether it's そうだ or らしい, it's something Hisa heard. And Hisa trusted it, and walked.

shared.text: どれだけ確かかを言い間違えると、話が全部信用できなくなるからね。
shared.en: Get how sure you are wrong, and nobody can trust any of it.

shared.text: 名札を、合う足跡に置いていこう。
shared.en: Let's set each name tag by the prints that match.

shared.text: 見た、聞こえた、聞いた、思った。分けてみると、狐の話は一枚も「見た」に入っていないね。
shared.en: Seen, heard, told, guessed. Sorted, not one slip about the fox is in "seen".

shared.text: 頼みの言葉、もう一度言おうか？
shared.en: Shall I say what she asked again?

shared.text: 頼まれたことをして、頼まれていないことはしない。それも、相手を大事にする方法だね。
shared.en: Doing what you're asked, and nothing you're not: that's a way of caring for someone, too.

shared.text: 囲炉裏の席にも、決まりがあるみたいだね。
shared.en: Even the seats round the hearth seem to have rules.

shared.text: 同じ注文が、門では仰せ、店ではご注文、家では「欲しいそうだ」になった。言葉は、相手に合わせて着替えるんだね。
shared.en: The same order was a decree at the gate, a commission at the shop and "he wants" at home. Words change their clothes to suit the listener.

shared.text: お客さんは客座。……今夜のあの人は、まだお客さんなんだね。
shared.en: The guest takes the guest's seat. …Tonight she is still a guest.

shared.text: 木尻に座るのは、家族になったしるしだね。
shared.en: Sitting by the firewood is a sign she has become family.

shared.text: 言葉は合っていても、相手を間違えると失礼になるんだね。
shared.en: The words can be right and still be rude, if they're aimed at the wrong person.

shared.text: 名札を、今夜の席に置いていこう。
shared.en: Let's set each name tag on tonight's seat.

shared.text: 奥さんには普通に、子供には優しく、店の人には丁寧に、殿さまの使いにはうんと丁寧に。同じ人が、四つの話し方をしていたね。
shared.en: Plain with his wife, gentle with a child, polite with the shopkeeper, very polite with the lord's man. One man, four ways of talking.

shared.text: 見えているのに、いないことにするのか。……声をかけてみよう。
shared.en: You can see it, and it counts as not there? …Say something to it.

shared.text: 意外な才能だな。
shared.en: An unexpected talent.

shared.text: 役の名前だけが消えている。役者の名前は残っているのに。
shared.en: Only the parts' names are gone. The actors' names are still there.

shared.text: 台詞を一緒に読んでみませんか。名前より先に、役が戻るかもしれない。
shared.en: Shall we read your lines together? The part might come back before the name does.

shared.text: 何でも治るは、何も治らないと同じかもね。
shared.en: "Cures everything" might be the same as "cures nothing".

shared.text: 森が、育ったんだね。
shared.en: The grove has grown.

shared.text: 一人で待つ灯じゃなくなったんだね。
shared.en: It isn't a lamp that waits alone any more.

shared.text: 一つは朝の合図だったみたいだよ。帳面を思い出そう。
shared.en: One stroke seems to have been the morning signal. Let's remember the notebook.

shared.text: 三つは夕方のヤギの合図だね。今は昼だよ。
shared.en: Three is the evening goat signal. It's noon now.

shared.text: ……吹雪の合図だよ、それ。みんなに謝りに行かないと。
shared.en: …That's the storm signal. We'll have to go round and apologise to everyone.

shared.text: 日誌は、あの大きな机の上だね。
shared.en: The log is on that big table.

shared.text: 少し休もう。あのストーブ、使えるかもしれない。
shared.en: Let's rest a bit. That stove might still work.

shared.text: 鍵が要る。机の上の書き置きに、何か書いてない？
shared.en: We need a key. Doesn't the note on the desk say something?

shared.text: $name、鐘の決まり、覚えてるよね？行こう！
shared.en: $name, you remember the bell rules, right? Let's go!

shared.text: デンジさんの言っていた、裏の階段でしょうか。中から開けられるはずです。
shared.en: That must be the back stair Denji mentioned. It should open from inside.

shared.text: 封を切らずに、透けて見える文だけ読めば……？
shared.en: What if we just read the lines that show through, without breaking the seals…?

shared.text: 扉の鍵はホシノさんが持っているはずです。先に話を聞きましょう。
shared.en: Hoshino should have the key to the door. Let's talk to him first.

shared.text: 向こう側からなら、開けられるかも。
shared.en: Maybe from the other side.

wordhelp.is: sentence-final question particle かい (a familiar, often older speaker's yes/no question)

examples.speaker: tsuru
examples.text: また行くのかい。道は、前とは違う顔をしているよ。
examples.en: Off again? The roads will have a different face from last time.

examples.speaker: tsuru
examples.text: そうかい。道は、逃げないよ。
examples.en: Suit yourselves. The roads aren't going anywhere.

examples.speaker: co_ume
examples.text: そのヤギかい。何年か前に、通りすがりの一座が置いていったのさ。「引退です」ってね。葉ばかり食べて、働きはしないよ。
examples.en: That goat? A passing troupe left it here a few years back. "Retired," they said. Eats leaves all day and never lifts a hoof.

examples.speaker: co_ume
examples.text: 植え付け帳、役に立ってるかい。変な頁があるだろう。若い木ばかり植えた年が。
examples.en: Is the planting book any use? There's an odd page in it, isn't there. The year we planted nothing but saplings.

wordhelp.is: やめる (止める: to quit, to stop doing), not 止む (rain stopping)

examples.speaker: ren
examples.text: 土の字。十の下に一。……字源の話は、やめておきます。嘘になるといけないので。
examples.en: The character for earth. A cross over a line… No, I'll leave the etymology alone. I don't want to make things up.

examples.speaker: pc
examples.text: やめておく
examples.en: Stay here

examples.speaker: nao
examples.text: 貼り替えたのはワタルだったな。俺たちが港長に話して、あいつも黙ってついて来た。黙っているのをやめたなら、十分だ。
examples.en: It was Wataru who swapped them. We told the harbourmaster, and he followed us in. If he's done keeping quiet, that's enough.

examples.speaker: pc
examples.text: やめておく
examples.en: Not now

wordhelp.is: つく as 付く / 点く / 吐く (嘘をつく, 気がつく, 名前がつく, ついて来る, 灯がつく), not "arrive"

examples.speaker: as_mitsue
examples.text: 名前がついたとたんに、手紙が一通届きましたよ。住所が書けるようになったからです。
examples.en: The moment the names were up, a letter arrived. Now people can write an address.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: 帳簿をいじった人がいるわね。数字は嘘をつかないけど、人はつく。……見つけたら、どうする？
examples.en: Someone's been fiddling the books. Numbers don't lie, but people do. …When we find them, what do we do?

examples.speaker: nao
examples.text: 貼り替えたのはワタルだったな。俺たちが港長に話して、あいつも黙ってついて来た。黙っているのをやめたなら、十分だ。
examples.en: It was Wataru who swapped them. We told the harbourmaster, and he followed us in. If he's done keeping quiet, that's enough.

examples.speaker: co_isao
examples.text: この火傷か。気がついたらあった。若い頃からな。
examples.en: This burn? It was just there one day. Since I was young.

wordhelp.is: な + explanatory んだ / んです, not 何 "what"

examples.speaker: co_kotaro
examples.text: ねえねえ、旅の人！祭り見に来たの？甘酒はね、子どもは一杯までなんだよ。ずるいよね。
examples.en: Hey, hey, travellers! You here for the festival? Kids only get one cup of amazake. Not fair, right?

examples.speaker: nao
examples.text: うわ、役所の匂いがする。俺、これ苦手なんだよな。
examples.en: Ugh, it smells like a government office. I can't stand these.

examples.speaker: akari
examples.text: ……父をご存知なんですか。
examples.en: …You know my father?

examples.speaker: akari
examples.text: 雪鈴の出なんです。父が山で星を見ています。
examples.en: I'm from Snowbell. My father watches the stars up on the mountain.

wordhelp.is: おかげ (お陰): thanks to

examples.speaker: mb_fujiko
examples.text: 灰実の里の干し柿が、うちに入るようになったよ。北の道が通ったおかげさ。
examples.en: Cinder Orchard's dried persimmons come to us now. All thanks to the north road being open.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: ……開いたわよ。あなたのおかげで、下は助かった。
examples.en: …It opened. Thanks to you, the village below was saved.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: ……開いたで。あんたのおかげで、下は助かった。
examples.en: …It opened. Thanks to you, the village below was saved.

examples.speaker: cr_tome
examples.text: 上から来た飛脚が、道の話を正しく持って来るようになったの。誰かさんのおかげね。
examples.en: The runners coming down have started bringing the road's news right. Thanks to someone, I think.

wordhelp.is: Kansai 〜へん after a て-form (〜てへん = 〜ていない), not 変 "strange"

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: 「伝えられている」。……正直な札やな。誰も数えてへんってことや。
examples.en: "Said to be." …An honest plaque. It means nobody's counted.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: ……ほんまは、怖かった。台本に書いてへん場面は、嫌いや。
examples.en: …Honestly? I was scared. I hate scenes that aren't in the script.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: 木の匂い、檜舞台を思い出すわ。杉も負けてへんけどな。
examples.en: The smell of wood takes me back to the big cypress stage. Cedar holds its own, though.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: ……自分の手紙は、まだ読んでもへんのにな。
examples.en: …When I haven't even read my own letter yet.

wordhelp.is: ふり (振り): pretending (分かったふり)

examples.speaker: nao
examples.text: 分からない、か。それが言えないと、分かったふりをするしかない。一番危ない道だ。
examples.en: "I don't know." Without it, you can only pretend you do. The most dangerous road there is.

examples.speaker: mio
examples.text: 一つずつ説明をつけて、全体を見ないふりをするのは、診察としては最悪です。
examples.en: Explaining every symptom separately so you never have to look at the whole patient — as a diagnosis, that's the worst there is.

examples.speaker: ko_yoshino
examples.text: アオが、朝の授業を窓の外から聞いているのです。……気付かないふりをしています。
examples.en: Ao listens to the morning lessons from outside the window. …I'm pretending not to notice.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: 黒子は、見えても見えないふりをするのが礼儀よ。……でも、ここは舞台じゃないわ。
examples.en: With a kuroko, it's good manners to pretend you can't see them. …But this isn't the stage.

wordhelp.is: a past ending after ん / 悪: 通れんかった, 悪かった, not 買う "buy"

examples.speaker: cr_genji
examples.text: 崖道へ行ってみたが、大きな石で通れんかった。馬を後ろへ歩かせて、戻って来たわい。
examples.en: I tried the ledge, but a big rock blocked it. I had to back the horse out and come home.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: ……さっきは、悪かったな。野暮なんて、言うつもりちゃうかったねん。手紙は、まだ怖くて開けへんだけや。
examples.en: …Sorry about earlier. I didn't mean to call you rude. It's only that I'm still too scared to answer the letter.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: 泣かへんかったんやな。立派な役者やで。帰ったら、拍手したるわ。
examples.en: You didn't cry. A fine performer. When we get home, I'll give you a round of applause.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: 十年、一座の帳面を付けてきた。誰にも見せへんかった。見せへんのが、自慢やった。
examples.en: I kept the troupe's books for ten years. I never showed them to anyone. I was proud nobody ever saw them.

wordhelp.is: ほんと (本当, casual): really

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: ……聞いただけよ。ほんとに。
examples.en: …Only heard. Really.

examples.speaker: mame
examples.text: ほんと？じゃあ、マメも字を練習する！自分で書けば、消えないよね！
examples.en: Really? Then Mame will practise writing too! If I write it myself, it won't disappear, right?

examples.speaker: chiyo
examples.text: 勝った！でも、ほんとはね、本物の灯りがつくほうが、うれしい。
examples.en: I won! But really… I'd be happier if the real lamp came on.

examples.speaker: rokuta
examples.text: キツネ、本物を見たんだ。雪の中からこっちを見てた。怖くなかった。……ほんとだよ。
examples.en: I saw a real fox. It was watching me from the snow. I wasn't scared. …Honest.

wordhelp.is: おふくろ: mum (a grown son's casual word)

examples.speaker: koji
examples.text: 渡し小屋を片付けてたら、おふくろの渡し帳が出てきた。誰を渡して、いくらもらったか、全部書いてある。
examples.en: I was tidying the ferry house and turned up Mum's fare book. Who she took across, what they paid — it's all written down.

examples.speaker: koji
examples.text: おふくろは死ぬまで、その客を待ってた。金のためじゃない。「払いに来るって約束したんだ。どこかで生きてるってことさ」ってな。
examples.en: Mum waited for that passenger till the day she died. Not for the money. "They promised to come and pay," she'd say. "That means they're alive somewhere."

examples.speaker: koji
examples.text: おふくろの帳面、最後の頁まで埋まった。新しい帳面を下ろしたよ。
examples.en: Mum's book is full to the last page now. I've started a new one.

examples.speaker: koji
examples.text: ……金はいい。おふくろは金を待ってたんじゃない。
examples.en: …Keep the money. Mum wasn't waiting for money.

wordhelp.is: かかり過ぎてる (掛かり過ぎている): costs too much

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: ねえ。一座に戻らないって決めたの、後悔してないわよ。元手がかかり過ぎてるって言ったけど。……本当は、一緒に舞台に立ちたい人に、久しぶりに会えたからよ。
examples.en: Listen. I don't regret deciding not to go back to the troupe. I said the investment was too great. …The truth is, it's the first time in ages I've met someone I want to share a stage with.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: なあ。一座に戻らへんって決めたの、後悔してへんで。元手がかかり過ぎてるって言うたけど。……ほんまは、一緒に舞台に立ちたい人に、久しぶりに会うたからや。
examples.en: Listen. I don't regret deciding not to go back to the troupe. I said the investment was too great. …The truth is, it's the first time in ages I've met someone I want to share a stage with.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: 元手がかかり過ぎてるの。ここまでの旅、ぜんぶ投資よ。今降りたら、大損。
examples.en: The investment's too great. This whole journey's been an investment. Get off now and I'd lose everything.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: 元手がかかり過ぎてるねん。ここまでの旅、ぜんぶ投資や。今降りたら、大損や。
examples.en: The investment's too great. This whole journey's been an investment. Get off now and I'd lose everything.

wordhelp.is: くじいた (挫いた): sprained

examples.speaker: hall_kota
examples.text: 「かずはとくいだけど、きのうあしをくじいたから、はこべない。」
examples.en: "I'm good at counting, but I twisted my ankle yesterday, so I can't carry."

examples.speaker: hall_kota
examples.text: 「数は得意だけど、昨日足をくじいたから、運べないんだ。」
examples.en: "I'm good at counting, but I twisted my ankle yesterday, so I can't carry."

examples.speaker: hall_kota
examples.text: 「足をくじいたせいで運べないけど、数えるのなら誰にも負けないよ。」
examples.en: "I'm good at counting, but I twisted my ankle yesterday, so I can't carry."

wordhelp.is: ござる: archaic polite "to be" (a deliberately old-fashioned speaker)

examples.speaker: cr_seibe
examples.text: 今夜はうちが満室でござる。松葉屋に、布団を借りに来た。
examples.en: We're full tonight. I've come to the Matsuba to borrow futons.

examples.speaker: cr_seibe
examples.text: 夜になったら、常夜灯の名を呼ぶ。「中山」とな。飛脚のまねでござるよ。
examples.en: At nightfall I call the lamp's name. "Nakayama." The way the runners did.

examples.speaker: cr_seibe
examples.text: 竹屋でござる。向かいの松葉屋より、風呂が熱い。
examples.en: This is the Take. Our bath is hotter than the Matsuba's across the way.

wordhelp.is: ございまして: polite て-form of ございます

examples.speaker: yn_okiyo
examples.text: ……申し訳ございません。ただいま、満室でございまして……。
examples.en: …We do apologise. We are fully booked at present…

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: 「満室でございまして」の後に、何も続かないのが、老舗の断り方よ。覚えておいて。
examples.en: "We are fully booked…" and then nothing after it: that's how an old house says no. Remember it.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: 「満室でございまして」の後に、何も続かへんのが、老舗の断り方や。覚えとき。
examples.en: "We are fully booked…" and then nothing after it: that's how an old house says no. Remember it.

wordhelp.is: 〜たびに (度に): every time

examples.speaker: nao
examples.text: あのすだれだな。鳴るたびに逃げてる。
examples.en: It's that screen. Every time it knocks, off it goes.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: 出番のたびに紙吹雪。本人は嬉しくないみたい。
examples.en: Confetti at every entrance. It doesn't seem pleased.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: 出番のたびに紙吹雪。本人は嬉しくないみたいやけど。
examples.en: Confetti at every entrance. It doesn't seem pleased.

wordhelp.is: Kansai おおきに: thank you

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: ……おおきに。相方があんたでよかったわ。
examples.en: …Thanks. I'm glad you're my partner.

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: ……おおきに、相方。久しぶりに、舞台で笑ったわ。間の取り方、悪くないで。
examples.en: …Thank you, partner. It's been a long time since I laughed on a stage. Your timing's not bad at all.

wordhelp.is: おまえ (お前): you (familiar or rough)

examples.speaker: hoshino
examples.text: 出ていく朝、わたしは約束した。あの灯りを、おまえが帰るまで消さない、と。
examples.en: The morning she left, I made a promise. That lamp won't go out until you come home.

examples.speaker: yae
examples.text: ホシノさんっていう天文学者がいてね。娘さんが灯落へ働きに出たとき、約束したんだって。「おまえが帰るまで、毎晩灯りをともしておく」って。
examples.en: There's an astronomer called Hoshino. When his daughter went down to work in Lanternfall, he made her a promise: "I'll keep the lamp lit every night until you come home."

wordhelp.is: しもうた = しまった (older western speech)

examples.speaker: mb_kansuke
examples.text: 儂のなぞなぞは、もう全部解かれてしもうた。……次に来るまでに、新しいのを考えておこう。
examples.en: You've solved every riddle I have. …By the time you come again, I'll have thought up new ones.

examples.speaker: mb_kansuke
examples.text: 新しいのも、全部解かれてしもうた。……まいった。儂の負けじゃ。
examples.en: You've solved the new ones too. …I give up. You win.

wordhelp.is: おまけ: an extra, a bonus

examples.speaker: tsuru
examples.text: 行くかどうかは、あんたたちの自由だ。物語はもう終わった。これは、おまけの散歩みたいなものだよ。
examples.en: Whether you go is entirely up to you. The story's over. Think of this as a bonus stroll.

examples.speaker: fuki
examples.text: ところがこのかぜで、柱に上れない。おまけに、決まりを書いた柱の板が、真っ白になっちまった。
examples.en: But with this cold I can't climb the post. And on top of that, the board with the rules on it has gone blank as snow.

wordhelp.is: やけに: awfully, strangely

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: 昔、一座で一度だけ来たことがあるんだ。鐘の音が、やけにきれいな村だった。
examples.en: I came here once with the troupe, years ago. A village where the bell sounded ridiculously clear.

examples.speaker: omi
examples.text: 荷の行き先を追ってくれ。油を待っていた灯台、灰が届かないガラス工房。それと市場のキヨだ。キヨは最近、やけに安い塩を仕入れたらしい。
examples.en: Follow the cargo. The lighthouse that was waiting for oil. The glassworks that never got its ash. And Kiyo at the market — she's been buying suspiciously cheap salt lately.

wordhelp.is: すまない (済まない): sorry

examples.speaker: cr_tatsu
examples.text: ……宿のことは、すまない。松葉屋に泊まるはずが、夜遅く着いて、開いていた竹屋に入ったんだ。
examples.en: …About the inns, I'm sorry. I meant to stay at the Matsuba, but I got in late and went into the Take, which was still open.

examples.speaker: hoshino
examples.text: ……おや。郵便かね。いや、冬に郵便は来ないな。すまない、癖でね。
examples.en: …Oh. Is that the post? No — no post comes in winter. Forgive me. Habit.

wordhelp.is: ざわざわ: uneasy stirring (mimetic)

examples.speaker: co_fusa
examples.text: トキワさんが、夕方広場に集まれって。何の話かしら。胸がざわざわするの。
examples.en: Tokiwa wants everyone in the square at dusk. I wonder what it's about. My chest feels all fluttery.

examples.speaker: lf_yae
examples.text: ……変ですね。読んでいたら、胸がざわざわする。昔の議会の夜みたい。
examples.en: …How odd. Reading this, my chest is all astir. Like a council night in the old days.

wordhelp.is: つまんない = つまらない (casual): boring

examples.speaker: lf_kei
examples.text: うそ。いいよ。大人はみんな「もちろん」しか言わないから、つまんないの。
examples.en: Just kidding. Okay. The grown-ups only ever say "of course". It's boring.

wordhelp.is: だんだん: gradually

examples.speaker: lf_yae
examples.text: カサネには、毎週手紙を書いています。毎回、向こうの意見に反対してね。返事は、字がだんだん揺れてきました。
examples.en: I write to Kasane every week, and disagree with them every time. Their replies — the handwriting's started to wobble.

wordhelp.is: じゃろう = だろう (older western speech)

examples.speaker: mb_zenzo
examples.text: 壁を崩せる者はおらんかのう。荷運びなら、力があるじゃろうに。
examples.en: Is there no one who can knock that wall through? A porter would have the strength.

wordhelp.is: じゃんけん: rock-paper-scissors

examples.speaker: suzu
examples.text: 共同演出ね。……意見が割れたら、じゃんけんで決める。それが一座の伝統。
examples.en: Co-directing. …If we disagree, rock-paper-scissors. Troupe tradition.

wordhelp.is: 〜ちゃ = 〜ては (casual): if you (do)…

examples.speaker: nao
examples.text: ……ああ。飛脚が手紙に隠れてちゃ、話にならない。
examples.en: …Yeah. A courier hiding behind a letter makes no sense.

wordhelp.is: ごちゃまぜ: a jumble

examples.speaker: hall_omatsu
examples.text: 十年預かっていた箱が、一晩で消えました。皆の話を紙に書いたけれど、見た話と聞いた話が、ごちゃまぜで。分けてもらえますか。
examples.en: A box I'd kept for ten years has vanished overnight. I wrote down what everyone said, but what they saw and what they only heard are all jumbled. Would you sort them?

wordhelp.is: ひとたまりもない: (would not last) a moment

examples.speaker: mio
examples.text: この茨、枯れてカラカラです。火がついたら、ひとたまりもない。
examples.en: These brambles are bone dry. One spark and they'd go up like paper.

wordhelp.is: まし: better (of two poor choices)

examples.speaker: mio
examples.text: 私が読むわ。濡れた薬の袋よりは、ましよ。何が知りたいの？
examples.en: I'll read it. Better than a wet medicine packet. What do you want to know?

wordhelp.is: おきょう (お経): sutras

examples.speaker: hall_koun
examples.text: 「たびのとちゅうです。おきょうのはこをせおっています。」
examples.en: "I'm a pilgrim on the road, carrying a box of sutras to a temple far away."

wordhelp.is: あいにく: unfortunately

examples.speaker: hall_koun
examples.text: 「連れの巡礼と二人です。あいにく、提灯の火は風に消されてしまいましたが。」
examples.en: "There are two of us pilgrims. Our lantern blew out in the wind, I'm afraid."

wordhelp.is: つった (攣った): got a cramp

examples.speaker: lw_cr_runner
examples.text: 足がつった。伝言を忘れそうだ。聞いて、言ってみてくれ。合っていれば、頭に戻る。
examples.en: Cramp. And I'm about to lose the message. Hear it and say it back to me. If you get it right, it'll stick again.

preserve.speaker: tsuru
preserve.text: 年寄りは回りくどいものさ。
preserve.why: Dry elder plain answering Nao's 「回りくどい」, and it makes the rule exposition self-aware. Keep both the 〜ものさ and Nao's bluntness.

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: レンと申します。川上から、嵐のあとの灯りを直しに来ました。灯守です。一応。
preserve.why: Ren's humble 申します to a stranger undercut by a deadpan 一応. This is the politeness-as-character Robin wants kept; do not flatten it.

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: 片付ける？人の手紙を？……失礼ですが、あなたの規定、間違っています。
preserve.why: Mio's temper with condescension, delivered through cold politeness to a hostile official. 失礼ですが plus あなた is exactly right here; making it casual would lose the bite.

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: 子ども扱いされるのが、一番嫌いなの。薬を調合して十五年よ。飴って。飴って！
preserve.why: Natural, heated soft-plain banter with repetition and ellipsis. Real speech, not textbook sentences.

preserve.speaker: tsuru
preserve.text: 行っておいで。名前を取り戻しておいで。
preserve.why: Warm elder 〜ておいで send-off. Marked but exactly right for Tsuru and the moment.

preserve.speaker: sg_clerk
preserve.text: 窓口は一つ。順番を守れ。次。
preserve.why: Clipped bureaucratic plain imperative. Stylised speech that defines the boss; it must not be softened or made literary.

preserve.speaker: mame
preserve.text: ……じゃあ、大きい声で言う。マメ！マメ！これで忘れないでしょ！
preserve.why: Mame's third-person self-reference is tied to the name-erasure theme (saying her name aloud so it won't vanish), not a generic child stereotype. Keep it.

preserve.speaker: suzu
preserve.text: さあさあ、旅のお方！嵐の夜の不思議な話、聞いていかない？お代は笑顔ひとつ！
preserve.why: Stage-barker formula over casual 聞いていかない？. The mock-honorific お方 is Suzu's performer voice. The Kansai version keeps the same register (聞いていかへん？…ええで).

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: 飴ではありません。薬です。膝が痛いのに平気な顔で階段を上る意地っ張りに、よく効くのもありますけど。
preserve.why: Mio's polite-to-strangers register used as a blade against condescension. The です/ます is what makes the barb funny, so it must not be made casual.

preserve.speaker: lq_chigusa
preserve.text: 嵐の夜に、お母さんに渡してもらった者です。遅くなりました。申し訳ありませんでした。
preserve.why: Dry, plain-spoken Chigusa switches to full formal apology for the one moment that calls for it, then goes back to her own voice in #6545e8f633 (分かってる。でも、払わせておくれ。). The shift is a deliberate model of register by situation.

preserve.speaker: lq_kayo
preserve.text: 鐘が鳴ってから、言えるようになったんです。……故郷の名前を忘れたのが、悲しい。悲しいです。言えて、よかった。
preserve.why: The plain 悲しい followed by the polite 悲しいです is her finding her voice. The repetition and the register step are the point and should survive any tidying.

preserve.speaker: nagisa
preserve.text: 意味分かんない。
preserve.why: Nagisa is family-casual with her father (なんで下にいるの / 意味分かんない / 来てくれて、ありがとう) and polite to the PC in the same scene (#fb1fdc224e …方ですよね). It shows register changing with the addressee.

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: イカはいかが。……失礼しました。
preserve.why: Ren's deadpan pun followed by a formal apology. Their politeness is the comedy here, and the same goes for 今回は、私が迷ったわけではありませんよ (sg.road_inland_closed#7df092f4c2) and 念のため (lq.road_loops#7feb9eb867).

preserve.speaker: omi
preserve.text: 言い訳をしろ。聞くのも、港長の仕事だ。
preserve.why: Brisk plain authority that is fair rather than harsh. Ōmi's short plain sentences to her subordinate are exactly right and should not be softened into polite speech.

preserve.speaker: nao
preserve.text: ……言えたじゃん。一番重い荷物は、下ろす直前が一番重いんだよ。
preserve.why: Nao's casual じゃん to an upset stranger reads as kindness, not rudeness. It is short, wry and in character.

preserve.speaker: lq_kayo
preserve.text: ……行きます。今度は、「もちろん」じゃなくて。行きたいから、行きます。
preserve.why: It pays off her compulsive polite もちろん (lq.kayo_idle, lq.road_kayo_certainly). The plain 「もちろん」じゃなくて inside the polite frame is natural and moving.

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: 正直に申し上げます。段々畑で、同じ柿の木の前を三回通りました。
preserve.why: The humble keigo 申し上げます, used to a friend to confess getting lost, is the joke. Ren's formality as deadpan character comedy must not be flattened.

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: 窯の中でも、私は構いません。……今のは聞かなかったことにしてください。
preserve.why: The 窯／構いません pun only works in Ren's careful polite form. The polite follow-up request is the punchline.

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: 誰かの大切な席なんだと思うよ。座らないでおこうね。
preserve.why: Mio, polite with the player and with strangers, drops to soft plain speech (〜よ, 〜おこうね) for a child. This is exactly the addressee-driven register shift Robin wants kept.

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: ……知らないうちに火傷をする人は、いません。
preserve.why: Polite, quiet and immovable toward a gruff elder: Mio's stubborn honesty delivered in です/ます. A casual rewrite would lose the steel.

preserve.speaker: co_tomoe
preserve.text: いい、今はいい。……ヒロ、おいで。頭にこれを巻いておきな。火の粉が熱いからね。
preserve.why: Plain, warm, decisive speech from a mother in an emergency (おいで, 〜ておきな, からね). This is the line Suzu and the village echo afterwards. Keep the wording, and add learner support instead of changing it.

preserve.speaker: co_heita
preserve.text: ……ん？あ、寝てませんよ。目を閉じて考えてただけっす。
preserve.why: The mix of ません and っす is exactly a lazy junior's casual-polite register toward strangers. Normalising it to either full polite or plain would erase Heita.

preserve.speaker: co_fusa
preserve.text: いらっしゃい。フサの宿へようこそ。茶屋もやってるから、甘酒でもどうぞ。
preserve.why: Country-inn hospitality: fixed polite phrases (いらっしゃい, ようこそ, どうぞ) wrapped around warm casual speech to a guest. A 'shopkeeper must use です/ます' rewrite would make her a chain hotel.

preserve.speaker: nao
preserve.text: 聞くなら、年寄りと職人だ。段々畑のばあさん、櫓のじいさん、ガラス工房の親方。
preserve.why: Nao's blunt ばあさん/じいさん sits against Mio's 「長く住んでいる方に」 and Ren's さん in the same slot (#7ae75703db, #6d196947a2). This is a clean demonstration of companion voices that should not be harmonised.

preserve.speaker: co_ume
preserve.text: おや、旅の人。段々畑は初めてかい。坂が急だから、足元に気をお付け。
preserve.why: Warm elder plain speech with かい and the motherly お付け is exactly right for Ume greeting strangers. Do not normalise it to です/ます or to standard 気をつけて.

preserve.speaker: hiro
preserve.text: それと……あんたは、隣に座れ。祭り二十回分、貸してある。一回ずつ返してもらう。
preserve.why: Terse plain imperatives with あんた: forgiveness given gruffly in Suzu's own ledger terms. Softening it would kill the moment.

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: 一つずつ説明をつけて、全体を見ないふりをするのは、診察としては最悪です。
preserve.why: Mio's fierce temper delivered in correct です/ます to an official: angry but still polite, and in her own professional idiom. It must not become plain or rude.

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: 火の前では、道を間違えません。動かないからです。
preserve.why: Ren's deadpan humour lives in the careful polite form. A casual version would lose the joke.

preserve.speaker: suzu
preserve.text: 来たこと？あるある。百回くらい。柿を食べに。
preserve.why: A natural casual deflection (echo question, doubled あるある, fragments) right before her confession. This is how real banter sounds.

preserve.speaker: co_tokiwa
preserve.text: 開村から百二十年、一年も欠けていません。字が汚い年はありますが。私の見習い時代など。
preserve.why: Formal polite with a dry self-deprecating tail: correct, burdened, human. It is FROZEN (VA1:NPC08_2) and a good model of polite speech that is not stiff.

preserve.speaker: co_sayo
preserve.text: 立派ですとも！百二十年、一度も休んだことがないんです。雨の年も、不作の年も。
preserve.why: Bright hostess politeness (ですとも, んです) to newcomers. Her later easy mix of です/ます with わ/のよね is her consistent voice, not an error.

preserve.speaker: nao
preserve.text: ……届いたな。二十年遅れの配達だ。受取人の返事まで、込みで。
preserve.why: Short, wry, plain, in courier metaphor: Nao's voice at its best, and an emotional beat without speechifying.

preserve.speaker: hoshino
preserve.text: ……おや。郵便かね。いや、冬に郵便は来ないな。すまない、癖でね。
preserve.why: Gentle elderly かね and a self-correction that sounds like a real person thinking aloud. It shows age without caricature (no わし/じゃ). Do not 'standardise' かね away.

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: ……ずるいなあ。そういうことを、暗い部屋で言うのは。顔が見えないから、信じるしかないじゃない。
preserve.why: Mio's soft plain register with the player at the emotional peak. The drop from です/ます is the point of the scene and must not be re-politened.

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: 座ってください。話はそれからです。断っても無駄ですからね。
preserve.why: Here politeness works as firmness: Mio's courteous です/ます to Kasane carries her fierce temper. Making it casual would lose the bite.

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: 「あかり」が、あかりをともしている。……今のは駄洒落ではありません。事実です。
preserve.why: Ren's deadpan pun works because of the formal denial; the polite register is the joke.

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: ……その可能性は、検討いたしかねます。
preserve.why: A deliberate piece of bureaucratic keigo used as a joke, tied to the game's 'vague words' theme (see 検討します。善処します。 in sa.b_ren4). It should not be removed as 'corporate phrasing'.

preserve.speaker: yae
preserve.text: 雪見屋のヤエです。部屋なら空いてるよ。冬はいつも空いてるけどね。
preserve.why: A natural innkeeper pattern: polite self-introduction, then warm casual at once. A good model of mixed register within one turn.

preserve.speaker: sousuke
preserve.text: 冬の郵便屋の仕事は、待つことです。得意ですよ。
preserve.why: Polite with a dry joke, exactly his profile; the です/ます are friendly, not stiff.

preserve.speaker: suzu
preserve.text: 吹雪の音って、拍手に似てない？鳴り止まない拍手。……嘘。ぜんぜん似てない。怖いだけ。
preserve.why: Real casual banter: a question with rising 〜ない？, a fragment, then she takes it back. The Kansai version keeps the same casual register (似てへん？…怖いだけや).

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: ごめんなさい。お断りします。葦ノ瀬に、店がありますので。
preserve.why: A textbook-right polite refusal to Councillor Tami, followed at once by plain to the player (#f2c3f9665b ……聞いた？今の。断った。ちゃんと、丁寧に。). The contrast between addressees is the whole point and must survive.

preserve.speaker: tsuru
preserve.text: 帰ったかい。顔を見せてごらん。……うん。道の顔になったね。
preserve.why: Elder warmth carried by かい／ごらん／ね with no stock じゃ. Exactly Tsuru's dry, kind voice.

preserve.speaker: sa_oyone
preserve.text: 下るのかい。お茶は飲んだね。よし。気をつけて行きな。
preserve.why: Brisk old-woman plain with the 〜な imperative and short checks. Natural hospitality, not caricature.

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: 失礼しました。今のは、解説の要らないほうの駄洒落です。
preserve.why: Ren's polite deadpan in the middle of a tragic scene. The formality is the joke and the character; don't flatten it.

preserve.speaker: akari
preserve.text: ……何のことでしょう。私は、なにも申しておりませんよ。
preserve.why: Humble keigo used as a wink while she slides the key across. It shows keigo doing social work, the opposite of stiffness.

preserve.speaker: hiro
preserve.text: スズ。座っていけよ。空いてる席の隣に。母さんの話、本当のほうを、もう一度聞かせてくれ。
preserve.why: Hiro says 母 to the outsider (#9f7b8ef2b8 席には、母の名前を彫った) and 母さん to his friend Suzu. A subtle, correct in-group/out-group shift.

preserve.speaker: lf_kei
preserve.text: ねえ！今は「いや」の上手な言い方を練習してるの。「遠慮しておきます」！
preserve.why: Cheeky child plain framing a quoted formal refusal. It teaches the register gap without a lecture.

preserve.speaker: nao
preserve.text: ……ああ。離すなよ。出口は、確かめなくていい。
preserve.why: Nao's rough-tender plain (なよ) in the most intimate moment, with the exits motif. Keep it casual.

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: ……お断りします。
preserve.why: Mio's first refusal to the Registrar has to be polite and formal: the point of the scene is a proper, courteous 'no'. Do not make it casual. The plain 「治療じゃない」 in #bebfe2f666 is also right as a moment of emphasis inside her polite speech.

preserve.speaker: lf_tadashi
preserve.text: 今なら申せます。承知いたしかねます。
preserve.why: Tadashi's humble keigo is the joke and the payoff together: he refuses in the most deferential form available. Keep 申せます and いたしかねます. His かしこ……。 cut-off (lf.mio_refuse#257b535df5) also depends on this register.

preserve.speaker: lf_ritsu
preserve.text: 本日、「虹色のお茶」はございません！……言えました！
preserve.why: Service keigo (ございません) used to refuse, followed by her own plain-polite delight. That is exactly how a timid café owner finds her voice. Keep both halves.

preserve.speaker: mb_fujiko
preserve.text: いらっしゃい。……客じゃないね。その顔は、外の騒ぎを見てきた顔だ。
preserve.why: A brisk merchant using plain speech to strangers is in character and natural for a busy 女将. Her うち (the house) versus 私 (herself) split is also right. Do not make her polite.

preserve.speaker: nao
preserve.text: 「おう」って言って、動かない。一番手強い断り方だよ、それ。
preserve.why: This is Nao at their best: short, wry, casual, with the afterthought それ tagged on the end. It is the model for ordinary banter in this part.

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: 名前は重荷ではありません。灯りです。返してもらいます。
preserve.why: Ren stays polite even in anger, which makes the line stronger. It is their character, not stiffness, and it must not be made plain to sound 'angrier'.

preserve.speaker: lf_tsuya
preserve.text: ……ふふ。怒るのって、久しぶり。甘酒が温まるわ。
preserve.why: Gentle older-feminine わ that grows out of who Tsuya is (patient, newly spirited), not a stock old-lady pattern. The humour depends on it.

preserve.speaker: suzu
preserve.text: 開演時刻の変更、承りました！
preserve.why: Suzu's stage call is deliberately polite and correctly unchanged in KANSAI. This is a model of keeping dialect separate from politeness.

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: ……私は、葦ノ瀬の薬師です。何が入っているか、言えますか？言えないなら、売らないでください。
preserve.why: Mio's temper in the face of condescension, delivered in cold, exact です/ます. The politeness is the weapon. Do not make it casual.

preserve.speaker: nao
preserve.text: 落としたことはある。拾っただけだ。
preserve.why: Nao in two short plain sentences: wry and honest, with no ceremony. A model of natural casual speech.

preserve.speaker: nao
preserve.text: ……なんだ、その謝り方。役所か。……でも、気持ちは届いた。
preserve.why: The register-teaching beat works: the companion reacts naturally to the pc's over-formal 誠に申し訳ありませんでした. Mio's ふふ、堅すぎですよ and Suzu's 殿様か！ in the same scene also work.

preserve.speaker: kr_hisae
preserve.text: 喧嘩かい。灯の前で喧嘩をすると、灯が曲がるって、昔は言ったもんさ。仲直りしておいで。
preserve.why: Sharp, kind elder speech (かい, もんさ, おいで) that is right for this person, not a generic granny. Keep the marked forms and add a learner note instead.

preserve.speaker: kr_juzo
preserve.text: 都から来た学者のジュウゾウです。この道の碑を、全部写しているところでして。
preserve.why: The scholar's trailing 〜でして, and 〜困りますがね in the next line, give a precise, slightly fussy politeness that defines him. Frozen VA2.

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: ……私は、その最後の灯守にはなりません。終わらせる灯守になります。
preserve.why: Ren's careful 私 + ません/ます is right for a vow. Formal here is character and moment, not stiffness.

preserve.speaker: sousuke
preserve.text: 待つのが得意な郵便屋ですが……待たせないのも、悪くないですね。
preserve.why: Sousuke's dry joke in polite form is his signature, and the reason ko.back_sb's plain lines stand out.

preserve.speaker: suzu
preserve.text: ……人の懐を覗くのは、野暮よ。客は舞台を見ていればいいの。
preserve.why: Suzu deflects through stage metaphor even in anger, with plain feminine endings. It is natural and character-specific in both standard and Kansai (野暮やで / 見とったらええねん).

preserve.speaker: omi
preserve.text: ゴホン。これより、面接を始めます。
preserve.why: Brisk, plain Ōmi switches into examiner keigo for the interview and then drops it ('合格だ。……ああ、肩が凝った。試験官の喋り方は、性に合わないよ。'). This register-teaching moment works naturally and must not be flattened in either direction.

preserve.speaker: nao
preserve.text: （……急に言葉が硬くなったな。）
preserve.why: The companion asides here (Nao's, plus Ren's '試験の言葉ですね。丁寧に答えましょう。') are in-scene register notes. They are exactly the kind of contextual support the spec asks for.

preserve.speaker: nao
preserve.text: ……大事に、預かります。
preserve.why: This is Nao's only です/ます in the part, said to a widow handing over her late husband's boat. Ceremony-averse Nao choosing politeness here is character, and it must not be 'corrected' to casual.

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: 壊すつもりはありません。話を聞かせてください。
preserve.why: Mio's polite, firm register with a hostile elder stranger is exactly her profile (です/ます to strangers, stubbornly honest).

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: ……ごめん、泣いてないよ。潮の水が、目に入っただけ。
preserve.why: Mio's softened plain speech with the player at an emotional peak. This is the intended closeness, and her cr lines should be brought into line with it, not the reverse.

preserve.speaker: ko_kihei
preserve.text: 手紙は、お前さんに任せる。俺には、もう決められない。
preserve.why: The old sailor's 'お前さん' is warm and of its generation, not rude. Changing it to あなた would kill the voice.

preserve.speaker: cr_ujie
preserve.text: ……雲居のシズ様の字と印。確かに。関をお通しいたします。お二人とも。
preserve.why: Ujie's humble official keigo ('お通しいたします') is correct and is his 'formal to the last syllable' character. It makes a good contrast with Gonza's archaic '待たれよ'.

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: ゲンタさん。……お疲れさまでした。
preserve.why: Ren's careful politeness, aimed at a ghost who kept faith for fifty years, is earnest and precise without being oracle-like. This is Ren at their best.

preserve.speaker: yn_tahei
preserve.text: 敬語で殴るのが、上の湯の流儀か！
preserve.why: The scene is built on the clash of Oritsu's icy でございます and Tahei's rough plain (来ねえんだよ, 冷てえ). Neither side may be levelled: the register gap is the joke and the conflict.

preserve.speaker: nao
preserve.text: ……久しぶりです、サキチさん。
preserve.why: Nao's rare です to the old courier who raised them on the road, then a fall straight back into plain (届いてはいた…). The stiffness of that one greeting says more than any line of exposition. Do not make it plain.

preserve.speaker: cr_ujie
preserve.text: 残る方は、番所でお預かりいたします。縄も牢もございません。お茶と座布団だけでございます。
preserve.why: Formal-to-the-last-syllable keigo as character, with dry humour inside it. It is also the model the interview challenge teaches. Keep the でございます.

preserve.speaker: suzu
preserve.text: 十六の時、毎晩真似しました。間の取り方を。……似てないって、皆に言われましたけど。
preserve.why: Suzu, plain with everyone, switches to です/ます when she meets her idol, and he answers with warm plain 君の間だ. That shift is right for the relationship and the moment.

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: キクエさん。……ご無沙汰しています。手紙の返事も、出さないままで。
preserve.why: Mio's polite, slightly guilty ご無沙汰しています to her mother's old friend, met by Kikue's motherly plain ミオちゃん？. It is exactly the right register pairing.

preserve.speaker: suzu
preserve.text: 「満室でございまして」の後に、何も続かないのが、老舗の断り方よ。覚えておいて。
preserve.why: An in-character register note: Suzu reads the inn's trailing keigo refusal for the player. It is the kind of contextual register comment the spec asks for, delivered in her voice.

preserve.speaker: yn_bunkichi
preserve.text: 按摩のブンキチでござい。……肩が凝っておいでだね。足音で分かる。
preserve.why: Old patter (でござい) with honorific-casual おいでだね: a specific tradesman's voice, not a generic old man. It needs a note, not normalising.

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: 「追分」。……灯よ、名を思い出してください。
preserve.why: The keeper's ritual address (vocative 灯よ, 名) inside Ren's courteous ください. It is ritual register used where ritual belongs, and should stay identical across the seven lamps.

preserve.speaker: nao
preserve.text: 丁寧に謝るなよ。余計に居心地が悪い。
preserve.why: Nao reacts to the player choosing the polite apology. It teaches that です/ます between close friends creates distance, and only works if Nao stays plain.

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: ……$nameさん。私は大丈夫です。今夜は、ここにいます。先に休んでください。
preserve.why: Mio's sudden さん and です here are a deliberate step back, and she names it herself the next morning (「大丈夫」と言って、扉を閉めました). It must not be 'normalised' to her softer speech.

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: ……古い決まりを、軽く見ないでください。それしか残っていない人もいるんです！
preserve.why: Ren stays polite even when angry, and the politeness carries the anger. This is character, not stiffness.

preserve.speaker: yn_oritsu
preserve.text: 拝見しておりました。断り方が、上手でいらっしゃる。
preserve.why: Oritsu's polished keigo is a weapon and a compliment at once (Suzu: 完璧な敬語で、相手の宿を刺す). Her でございます / でいらっしゃる speech must stay exactly this formal.

preserve.speaker: yn_oritsu
preserve.text: 露天風呂のことは、来月の寄合で、また申し上げるつもりでございます。……楽しみにしておりますのよ。少しだけ。
preserve.why: 〜ておりますのよ is old-fashioned upper-class speech, which makes her dry playfulness land.

preserve.speaker: yn_tahei
preserve.text: ……入れてないとは言ってねえ。土間に寝てるのが、六人いる。金は取ってねえ。言うなよ。
preserve.why: Tahei's rough ねえ against Oritsu's keigo is the scene's whole contrast between the two houses. Neither should be evened out.

preserve.speaker: tsuru
preserve.text: おや、終わったかい。待ちくたびれたよ。
preserve.why: This is the right elder voice: dry and plain, with かい and よ and no stock 〜じゃ, as the brief asks.

preserve.speaker: mp_tokube
preserve.text: さあさあ、本場の名薬だよ！……おや、どこかで見た顔だね。八百橋の芝居町かい？
preserve.why: Authentic hawker's patter (さあさあ, 〜だよ, 〜かい). It is stage-flavoured speech that belongs to this character.

preserve.speaker: nao
preserve.text: 傘が……立ってる。目が一つある。……見なかったことにしていいか？
preserve.why: Exactly Nao: wry, clipped, a natural contraction (立ってる) and self-interrupting beats. Do not tidy it into complete sentences.

preserve.speaker: hall_ibuki
preserve.text: ……「例外はない」と書いたのは、私だ。怖かったんだ。間違えるのが。
preserve.why: Clipped plain with 私 and an afterthought inversion (間違えるのが): a natural spoken confession and the core of Ibuki's rule-bound, anxious voice.

preserve.speaker: hall_kihei
preserve.text: 腰を痛めてな。関所は、イブキに任せてある。……真面目すぎるのが、玉に瑕じゃがな。
preserve.why: Dry, affectionate folk-tale elder. It needs a learner note, not standardisation; not every elder in the Hall talks like this (Jinbei is plain だ, Kyūbei polite), so it reads as Kihei's own voice.

preserve.speaker: hall_koun
preserve.text: ありがとうございます。二人で、足元に気を付けて行きます。
preserve.why: Humble polite fits a pilgrim at a checkpoint and gives the learner a polite model among the plain-speaking travellers.

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: 鐘は、時を告げるものです。告げられたくない誰かが、いるのでしょう。
preserve.why: Ren's careful です/ます to the player is character, not stiffness: precise, calm, a little ominous. It is the baseline the generic lines currently break.

preserve.speaker: hall_mataji
preserve.text: 火の用心の途中で、見たよ。小さいのを。
preserve.why: Real spoken word order, with the object added as an afterthought: plain, alert witness speech. Keep it rather than 'correcting' it to 小さいのを見たよ.

preserve.speaker: hall_mosuke
preserve.text: 任せておけ。
preserve.why: With Hatsu's 任せて。 and Kōta's 任せてよ。 the same phrase is given in three registers fitted to each person: a neat contrast to keep distinct.

preserve.speaker: suzu
preserve.text: KANSAI: 香盤表みたいなもんやな。任せとき。何を見るん？
preserve.why: The Kansai version keeps exactly the casual level of the standard line (もんね→もんやな, 任せて→任せとき). This is dialect without any change in politeness, as intended throughout this part.

preserve.speaker: hall_saki
preserve.text: 狐なんかじゃありません！私は、見たんです。
preserve.why: She stays polite to an older guest even while angry. It shows that polite does not mean calm, and the んです emphasis is exactly right.

preserve.speaker: hall_otoku
preserve.text: うちの人、今日は村じゅうで喋ってきたらしいけど、言葉を雪の中に落としてきたみたいでね。
preserve.why: Natural old-wife plain speech: うちの人, the trailing 〜みたいでね, and the joke carried in ordinary words.

preserve.speaker: hall_yosaku
preserve.text: 今日は村の皆に声をかけて回ったんだが、誰に何を言ったか、すっかり分からなくなってしまってな。言葉を、言った相手に返してくれんか。
preserve.why: A kindly old man without the じゃ cliché (〜んだが, 〜てな, くれんか). It stays distinct from Gonroku's deliberate role language.

preserve.speaker: hall_gensuke
preserve.text: はて、そんな言い方は、私にはなさいませんでしたよ。
preserve.why: Merchant courtesy: he uses an honorific for a third party (なさる) while correcting the player gently. It is a fine model of polite disagreement.

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: あの方の頼みは、私が伺いました。何をお話ししましょうか。
preserve.why: Ren's careful keigo (伺う toward the crane-girl, お話しする) is character, not stiffness. Do not flatten it, and use it as the reference when fixing the generic lines Ren has to voice.

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: 迷った回数も、全部数えてあります。公表はしません。
preserve.why: The deadpan joke depends on the polite register. A casual version would lose the humour.

preserve.speaker: nao
preserve.text: それに、五日に一度は潮硝子回りの配達がある。暇なら、荷物を半分持て。
preserve.why: A blunt imperative (持て) as affection between partners is exactly Nao. Do not soften it to 持ってくれる？.

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: いいの？じゃあ、重い方の鞄をお願い。……冗談。半分ずつにしよう。
preserve.why: Mio's softened plain speech with the player at the end of the game: natural fragments, a self-correction and a teasing tone. It shows the intended closeness.

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: ……札を付けたんですね。決めていないことに。
preserve.why: Mio stays polite to her elder Kikue while Kikue calls her ミオちゃん. The asymmetry is exactly right and should not be flattened to plain.

preserve.speaker: cr_gonza
preserve.text: いらっしゃい。関所はやめた。今は茶屋だ。手形は要らん。注文だけ聞く。
preserve.why: A former barrier guard running a teahouse in clipped guard-plain is the joke and the character. Do not 'correct' it to shop keigo.

preserve.speaker: suzu
preserve.text: では、見得を切ります！ / KANSAI: ほな、見得を切ります！
preserve.why: A model of dialect kept separate from politeness: the polite stage announcement stays 〜ます in Kansai, and only the opener changes (では→ほな).

preserve.speaker: ren
preserve.text: ……今日の冗談は、品切れです。明日入荷します。
preserve.why: Ren's deadpan comes from the politeness itself (shop-notice です/ます about jokes). Making it casual would kill the joke.

preserve.speaker: tsuru
preserve.text: そうかい。道は、逃げないよ。
preserve.why: Tsuru's dry plain elder voice with かい/よ, not 〜じゃ, as the brief specifies. It is short and natural.

preserve.speaker: kr_hisae
preserve.text: 一緒に歩くかい、レン。道を歩く灯守なら、もう迷わないだろう？
preserve.why: Sharp old-woman かい/だろう without caricature. Ren's polite reply (……約束はできません。) makes a good register contrast.

preserve.speaker: mio
preserve.text: はいはい、診察は終わり。元気でよろしい。
preserve.why: Mio's playful doctor-voice (よろしい) to an animal. It is a marked register used for fun, which shows her warmth.

preserve.speaker: nao
preserve.text: 出口は二つ。連れは一人。問題なし。
preserve.why: Nao's clipped, wry courier style. These fragments are natural speech, not textbook sentences.

speakerNotes.speaker: tsuru
speakerNotes.note: Consistent dry elder plain (だね／かい／〜な／おくれ／おいで), no じゃ. A good model. Needs learner notes for かい and おくれ, and おくれ should stay hers rather than spreading to younger NPCs.

speakerNotes.speaker: nao
speakerNotes.note: Clipped casual (だ／な／ぞ／〜しとけ, 俺／あんた) is consistent and natural throughout, including companion asides. Calling Tsuru 婆さん is in character. Nothing to change.

speakerNotes.speaker: mio
speakerNotes.note: Polite to the player in Reedwake, then soft plain from the Saltglass arrival (sg.arrive), which fits the intended softening. Problems: polite lines leak in from the case files and the Reedwake banter (rw.b_mio1, post-game rw.b_mio2). Elsewhere in the game she goes back to です／$nameさん in Cinder Orchard after plain/bare $name in Saltglass, so Robin should fix one arc for her register to the player. Her polite lines to NPCs (Genzō, Ōmi, the Clerk) are right.

speakerNotes.speaker: ren
speakerNotes.note: Careful です／ます with deadpan tags (一応／念のため／私が、です). Natural, not oracle-speak, with a few plain maxims that suit a keeper. Two consistency points: 先生 (Reedwake only) vs 師匠 (everywhere else). Also, Ren addresses the player by bare $name (sg.b_ren_puns), and in all 10 uses game-wide, never $nameさん. Combined with consistent です／ます that is an unusual mix; fine if deliberate, but worth a conscious decision.

speakerNotes.speaker: suzu
speakerNotes.note: Playful plain with stage formulas; the Kansai versions keep politeness level almost everywhere (only sg.check_clues diverges). Standard-line あたし (vs usual 私) appears only in money/debt lines (sg.b_suzu_accounts, sg.b_suzu_debt, and later sb.*). That reads as a deliberate slip into her down-to-earth self; keep it confined to those lines.

speakerNotes.speaker: pc
speakerNotes.note: Registers are well chosen by addressee: polite to Tsuru, Yasu, Genzō, Wataru, Seto, Hama and the Clerk; plain to Mame and to companions. Only the あなた宛 phrasing to Hama is stiff.

speakerNotes.speaker: hana
speakerNotes.note: Soft feminine casual (〜の／〜わ／〜よね) even to a stranger, which suits a warm village teahouse keeper. Uses あんた to her brother and あなた to the guest, which is correct. Only the 今朝 reading hazard needs fixing.

speakerNotes.speaker: sg_clerk
speakerNotes.note: Clipped bureaucratic plain with written-style chains (返送し、棚に上げ、静かにする). Right for a functionary boss; keep it.

speakerNotes.speaker: asahi
speakerNotes.note: Lively chatty casual (〜よね／〜んだ／ねぇ) with natural self-interruptions (……そっか). Good model banter.

speakerNotes.speaker: mio
speakerNotes.note: She is polite to strangers throughout and it works (Genzō, Ōmi, Tetsu, Chigusa, Kayo). Toward the PC she is plain for all of ch2 but polite in ch1, in lq lines like road_write and kayo_idle, and from ch3 co.arrive on. That swing needs one decision (see co.arrive#c99094f2db).

speakerNotes.speaker: nao
speakerNotes.note: Consistent wry plain with 俺/あんた in short sentences, natural throughout this part. Their courier metaphors recur often but stay conversational.

speakerNotes.speaker: ren
speakerNotes.note: Careful polite with plain, aphoristic thinking-aloud sentences (e.g. sg.harbor_first 嵐の夜だけのことではない。今も続いている。, sg.wataru_letter 本庁があるからこそ…). This is character, not stiffness, and the deadpan puns and getting-lost denials are the best of it. Nothing to fix here.

speakerNotes.speaker: suzu
speakerNotes.note: Standard voice is playful plain with わ/よ/ね and stage phrases, and the KANSAI versions keep the same politeness. はる is added naturally for third persons (覚えてはる, してはった). Watch あんた in standard lines (lq.road_write) and the 今のうち garden path in co.ashband KANSAI.

speakerNotes.speaker: shiori
speakerNotes.note: Her precise polite register fits, but she leans on written のです (いらっしゃったのですか, 止んでいるのです) and once narrates the word-help UI. Lighter spoken んです in ordinary turns would keep her precise without sounding read.

speakerNotes.speaker: yasu
speakerNotes.note: Gruff, tender and plain, which fits. In the lq quest only, he gains わし and 〜とった, which elsewhere he does not use (dv.yasu has 俺).

speakerNotes.speaker: lq_chigusa
speakerNotes.note: Dry plain with かい/さ/おくれ/おいき is consistent and well judged, and the one formal apology in lq.fare_pay is exactly placed. Her marked forms want register notes, not changes.

speakerNotes.speaker: omi
speakerNotes.note: Brisk plain to everyone, including the PC as a stranger, fits a harbourmaster. Her judgement scene with Wataru is a model of register and should be kept.

speakerNotes.speaker: pc
speakerNotes.note: Polite to elders and officials and casual to the companion, which is appropriate. Two lines use あなた to older named women (Chigusa, Kayo), and one choice to a child (今は急いでいる。) reads like narration.

speakerNotes.speaker: wataru
speakerNotes.note: Anxious polite 僕/です・ます, consistent and natural, including the fragments under stress in sg.wataru_confront. No issues.

speakerNotes.speaker: nao
speakerNotes.note: Consistently plain and rough (俺, あんた, お前 to Suzu) with courier metaphors. The register suits every addressee, including casual speech to elders, which is in character. The only issue in this part is continuity in co.b_nao4.

speakerNotes.speaker: mio
speakerNotes.note: Polite to the player throughout ch3, with plain observation fragments followed by polite explanations (焦げ目が深い。…んです), which is natural. She softens to plain with Kotarō. Two things to watch: 皆さん、 at the start of a sentence when she means the villagers (assembly, bell_ring, festival_begin), and one grading 「賢い」 to a stranger.

speakerNotes.speaker: ren
speakerNotes.note: Careful polite speech with humble keigo used deadpan (申し上げます, 承知しました): keep it. Almost every examine line in this chapter is a maxim (木は燃えたことを忘れません, 鐘を鳴らした腕は…, 水門の名は…, 道が、道であることを…). Each is fine alone, and the comic lines balance them, but Robin may want fewer if the 'oracle' concern applies.

speakerNotes.speaker: suzu
speakerNotes.note: Standard voice is plain with わ/わよ and stage metaphors, and it is consistent. The Kansai versions keep the politeness level, and 〜はる on third persons (言わはった) is deliberate per docs/dialect/suzu_kansai.md. Two Kansai forms need a native fix (立たんとな, せえへんでおく). The co.goat lines after :suzu are labelled ANY(comp) in the transcript but belong to Suzu and have Kansai versions in kansai_30_ch3.js: the recording script should cast them to Suzu.

speakerNotes.speaker: co_goro
speakerNotes.note: わし, おる and the 〜ん negative are used consistently and lightly, with no pile-up of じゃ. It reads as this rambling bell-keeper, not a caricature. 頼まれてくれんか needs a learner note.

speakerNotes.speaker: co_tokiwa
speakerNotes.note: Formal polite in public and with the player. The plain sentences at the emotional peak of his confession (でも静寂は、火事ごと持って行った) are natural. 旅のお方 is slightly period-drama, but acceptable for a formal recorder addressing an outsider in public.

speakerNotes.speaker: co_heita
speakerNotes.note: Mixes ません with っす (なんっす, っすよ) and switches to plain 持ってます in front of stern Tamotsu. The register is precise and should stay.

speakerNotes.speaker: co_kotaro
speakerNotes.note: Natural child speech (僕, ねえねえ, じゃん, contractions) in the authored scenes. Only the living-world lines lose the contractions.

speakerNotes.speaker: suzu
speakerNotes.note: Consistently playful plain speech (わ/の/よ, stage vocabulary), and the Kansai versions almost always keep her politeness. The はる on third parties (Sayo, Hiro, the keeper) is natural Kansai, not a register change. Exceptions: the polite Kansai line to Hiro (co.suzu_ask), the mock-polite ください that becomes ちょうだい, and the broken 目がない idiom. Her 君 to Hiro in co.suzu_truth is unique in her lines: confirm it is intended.

speakerNotes.speaker: nao
speakerNotes.note: Terse plain (だ/な/ぞ, 俺/あんた) throughout, with good wry courier metaphors. Nao is polite once, to Ume at first meeting, which is a nice touch, and that makes the later ばあさん to her face jar. One quip (にすぎない) drifts into written register.

speakerNotes.speaker: mio
speakerNotes.note: Polite to the player in every ch3 companion topic, including the post-game variants. In ch4 banter she mixes polite and soft feminine plain (〜ね/〜の/〜わ). The mix sounds like natural softening, and her polite fierceness with Tokiwa is right. Robin may still want to decide whether her register toward the player follows a deliberate trajectory, since the post-game topics are more polite than the ch4 banter.

speakerNotes.speaker: ren
speakerNotes.note: Careful polite speech with deadpan getting-lost jokes. The plain musings (星の名前まで……) are fine and in character. The only Ren problems in this part come from generic companion lines that would make Ren say だよ/だね/書いてない？.

speakerNotes.speaker: hiro
speakerNotes.note: Terse masculine plain (俺/あんた, 〜だ, 行っちまった) suits him and his confrontation scene is strong. Two idioms need attention: それは数える (calque) and 頭が白くなる (should be 真っ白).

speakerNotes.speaker: co_tokiwa
speakerNotes.note: Formal です/ます, with plain only in conjecture, self-talk and quoted thought (〜かもしれない, 見つかるはずがない). This is natural and consistent. One content slip: 鐘 should be 綱 in co.tokiwa_after.

speakerNotes.speaker: co_sayo
speakerNotes.note: Profile says 'bright polite', but from her first scenes on she mixes です/ます with feminine plain asides (わ, のよね, かしら). The adjacent shifts in co.sayo_seats are her consistent voice, so they are not flagged.

speakerNotes.speaker: co_ume
speakerNotes.note: Folksy elder plain (〜だよ, 〜さ, かい, お+stem imperatives, あんた). Natural and warm; it needs a register note for learners, not a change.

speakerNotes.speaker: fuki
speakerNotes.note: Dry elder plain (かい, 〜さ, おくれ, ちまった), close to Ume's markers but distinct in attitude. Realistic rather than caricature.

speakerNotes.speaker: co_tamotsu
speakerNotes.note: Blunt plain with imperatives (来い, 持って行け, 気をつけろ). Consistent, and right for a stern channel keeper speaking to outsiders.

speakerNotes.speaker: nao
speakerNotes.note: Consistently casual and wry (だ/な/ぜ, あんた to Hoshino and the player). Natural throughout. The one real problem is the subjectless 頼んだぞ in sa.after_battle, which reads as the set phrase.

speakerNotes.speaker: ren
speakerNotes.note: Polite to the player throughout chapter 4, with more plain-form observations in chapter 6. That fits 'careful, occasionally formal'. Problems are a handful of calques (これら, 一番美しい種類の, 精神にいい) and one definition-style line to Hoshino. The aphorisms at the lamp climax (名は灯に、灯は人に) are acceptable as ritual speech.

speakerNotes.speaker: mio
speakerNotes.note: Polite with Hoshino, Kasane and Oyone, which is right. Toward the player: polite in chapter 4 public scenes, plain in the night talk, then polite again in the next morning's dungeon before plain from chapter 5. Robin should place the softening deliberately.

speakerNotes.speaker: suzu
speakerNotes.note: Lively casual standard with stage phrases. The Kansai versions keep politeness level line-for-line in her own lines. In chapter 4 her standard first person switches to あたし and she once uses あんた, unlike the rest of the game. The two shared polite lines (stair_ice, service_door_out) are out of voice for her in standard mode.

speakerNotes.speaker: hoshino
speakerNotes.note: A gentle, consistent elderly plain voice (わたし, 君たち, かね/かい, 〜ておくれ), not a caricature. Only おくれ needs a learner note.

speakerNotes.speaker: kasane
speakerNotes.note: Courteous です/ます with plain fragments under emotion (曖昧な言葉で、最後まで。), which reads naturally. No issues found.

speakerNotes.speaker: yae
speakerNotes.note: Warm bustling casual with a polite self-introduction and かい/かしら touches. Natural. Only 禁止事項 sounds like an official notice.

speakerNotes.speaker: sa_clerk
speakerNotes.note: 当書記 plus です/ます is a well-judged character voice (lexicon has a note). Tsuzuri's switch to its own name is clear and should stay.

speakerNotes.speaker: tetsuji
speakerNotes.note: Gruff masculine with 〜ん negatives; consistent. 知らんで drifts into dialect, and the ん-negatives need a learner note because word help maps them to the positive verb.

speakerNotes.speaker: kanta
speakerNotes.note: Boyish casual (おれ, すげえ, 〜ちゃった) in the main scenes. The living-world lines (05_author.js) uncontract 〜ている and sound read-aloud; the same applies to Natsume and Sachi there.

speakerNotes.speaker: mio
speakerNotes.note: Mio's register is excellent through ch5 and ch6: です/ます to strangers and patients (Kasane, Isamu, Oyone, Tami, the customer) and soft plain to the player. The sa2 layer (hushed, end_mio, romance) reverts to です/ます toward the player inside scenes where she is otherwise plain, and that is the one systematic problem in this part.

speakerNotes.speaker: ren
speakerNotes.note: Ren's careful polite speech, with plain fragments for private realisation (……師匠の字だ。), works well; keep it. The density of free-standing maxims is high (lantern sayings in almost every scene). Keep the quoted teachings, but thin the self-made aphorisms in ordinary moments (lf.akari_reply, lf.bench_canal) and the lesson metalanguage (lf.east_door, and to a lesser degree the まで gloss in lf.fence_talk).

speakerNotes.speaker: nao
speakerNotes.note: Nao is consistently casual and short, with 俺 and 君 for Umi (consistent with lf.nao_deliver); no register problems. The only issue is the hybrid charter quotation in sa.mem_requests.

speakerNotes.speaker: suzu
speakerNotes.note: Suzu's standard voice (plain with わ/よ/の, stage calls, ledger jokes) is consistent. Her Kansai mostly keeps the standard line's politeness, with three exceptions: はる to Oyone, はがしたろ for the polite flourish, and the ambiguous 貸しちゃうで. Kansai 〜たる/〜たって/〜たない forms recur without learner support.

speakerNotes.speaker: kasane
speakerNotes.note: Kasane is courteous and articulate; plain self-talk in the realisation scene (sa.toya_read) mixed with polite address reads naturally. Only the remembered young-Kasane lines carry gendered endings, which conflicts with the they/them design.

speakerNotes.speaker: pc
speakerNotes.note: The PC is appropriately polite to strangers and officials and plain to children (lf.kei). With companions the PC is plain in ch2, ch3 and ch6 but polite in ch5 banter (lf.b_nao1, lf.b_mio1, lf.b_suzu2, lf.arrive), and that drift should be unified.

speakerNotes.speaker: sa_oyone
speakerNotes.note: Oyone, Tsuru and Tae all use plain elder speech with かい/な/さ/だね and no stock じゃ. They are distinct from one another and right as written.

speakerNotes.speaker: lf_kinu
speakerNotes.note: Kinu and Kōhei's exaggerated mutual politeness before the bell and blunt plain after it is the scene's mechanism and works. Kinu's ですわ is a deliberate genteel marker that needs a learner note, not a change.

speakerNotes.speaker: nao
speakerNotes.note: Consistently casual, short and wry, which is right throughout. The only wobble is the second-person pronoun: 君 to Umi (lf.nao_deliver, twice) and 君たち to the player (lf.naoc_after), where Nao otherwise uses あんた or no pronoun.

speakerNotes.speaker: mio
speakerNotes.note: Polite to strangers (Tadashi, Tsuya, Haru, Sen, Fujiko) and mostly plain with the player, as designed. A few quiet polite lines to the player (mb.ks_token_shelf, mb.sen_dispute, mp.boss_won, mp.chapter_end) match her game-wide habit of slipping into です/ます when reflective, and are not flagged.

speakerNotes.speaker: ren
speakerNotes.note: Careful polite with good deadpan (directions jokes, 「私の逆を行ってください」). The weak spots are a few English-shaped phrasings (師匠の残り, 同じ穴に落ちる, きれいにない) and one vocabulary lecture to the Registrar, not the politeness itself.

speakerNotes.speaker: suzu
speakerNotes.note: Plain, playful stage voice throughout, and the KANSAI lines are idiomatic (返し！, 見たない, 書いたろか). The one systematic issue: her standard 〜ましょう suggestions always become plain volitional in KANSAI.

speakerNotes.speaker: umi
speakerNotes.note: Controlled polite at the counter, with plain speech breaking through under emotion with Nao. The shifts in lf.nao_deliver are well motivated. The only questionable one is the return to です/ます with Nao in lf.umi_post.

speakerNotes.speaker: lf_tadashi
speakerNotes.note: Humble formal keigo (でございます, 申せます, 承知いたしかねます) is consistent and carries the Lanternfall theme. Keep it intact.

speakerNotes.speaker: mb_kansuke
speakerNotes.note: Old-man role language (儂, じゃ, しもうた, のう) in the riddle scenes, but neutral plain speech in mb.kansuke_night (lost child). That may be deliberate seriousness. If the voice is meant to be consistent, the night scene should keep one light marker.

speakerNotes.speaker: mb_zenzo
speakerNotes.note: Full stock old-man speech that his profile (warm, contented) does not call for, and that he applies inconsistently (茶を飲んだよ, ありがとうよ). It is the most stereotyped voice in this part.

speakerNotes.speaker: nao
