speakerNotes.note: Consistently plain, short and wry, with courier metaphors that land naturally. Nao is off-voice only where comp!=X lines (mp.saku_first, mp.tokube) force polite or soft endings onto them.

speakerNotes.speaker: mio
speakerNotes.note: Mixes です/ます with soft plain (のね, のよ) toward the pc. The shifts follow emotion (anger at Tokubē, the apology in kr.makeup, the angry 休めるわけないでしょう！…んですよ！) and read naturally. Do not regularise.

speakerNotes.speaker: ren
speakerNotes.note: Careful polite speech with deadpan humour (記録には書けませんね。書きたいですけど。), right throughout. Plain reflective lines (全部が正しいわけじゃなかった) are fine. Problems appear only in generic comp lines and one bookish のですよ to a child.

speakerNotes.speaker: suzu
speakerNotes.note: The standard voice is consistent: playful plain feminine, stage metaphors, and polite only for stage patter and solemn beats. The Kansai is mostly good, but has the non-native 〜たねん pattern (3 lines here), a few politeness drops relative to the standard line, and two おおきに that contradict the style sheet.

speakerNotes.speaker: kr_hisae
speakerNotes.note: Sharp elder plain (かい, さ, おくれ, お行き, おやり, おいで), never じゃ: well differentiated from Tsuru and Kame. It needs one learner note on the お〜 imperatives. (In passing, the word-help 'unexplained' list shows sentence-final かい parsed as counter 回 for her and other elders.)

speakerNotes.speaker: mp_tomi
speakerNotes.note: Brisk organiser: です/ます for requests and explanations to the helper, plain わ / のね for reactions, and ごらんなさい / ちょうだい warmth. The mixture is natural and should be kept.

speakerNotes.speaker: mp_manbe
speakerNotes.note: Showman's polite with plain exclamations under stress (奈落だ！, 芝居が、動いた！), which is fine. Only ko.back_mp drifts to plain requests.

speakerNotes.speaker: any
speakerNotes.note: The four comp!=X lines in mp (kuroko_meet, manzai, saku_first, tokube) are all written in one voice, usually Nao's. The mp.fireworks and mp.stagedoor 'any' lines are in fact companion-specific and correctly voiced in the source.

speakerNotes.speaker: ko.back_* round (sousuke, asahi, co_ume, mp_manbe)
speakerNotes.note: The 'words came back' vignettes in ko/21_scenes_village.js read as batch-written: four of the eight speakers drift from their established register or voice. One pass over the set against each speaker's other lines would catch them together.

speakerNotes.speaker: mio
speakerNotes.note: Mio's register towards the player depends on the region: in ko (ch9) she is softly plain, as in lf (ch5), but in cr (ch10) almost every companion line goes back to です/ます (arrive1–6, barrier_first, bridge, barrier_back, call), and the sea/sz/el lines are mostly polite as well. Her polite lines to strangers (Nami, Kihei, Genroku, Chika, Isaku, Fuku) are right. A few ko lines to the player are polite in plain-speech surroundings (ko.hall_exhibit 'ものですね'), which is a minor wobble.

speakerNotes.speaker: suzu
speakerNotes.note: Standard Suzu is consistently plain and playful with stage metaphors; it is good and never tips into oracle-speak. Her Kansai versions mostly keep the register. Two things to fix: the 〜かったねん past form (ko.suzu_leaf, and the same pattern in other Kansai files), and the uneven handling of 〜ましょ(う) (sometimes kept, sometimes turned into plain volitional).

speakerNotes.speaker: nao
speakerNotes.note: Nao is consistent: short plain lines with courier metaphors, 俺, the occasional ぞ. The one polite line (sea.fuku_hull) is a deliberate shift for the moment. Nothing to fix.

speakerNotes.speaker: ren
speakerNotes.note: Ren's polite, precise voice holds throughout. The ko toro (old kana) explanations sit in Ren-only branches (after ':ren'), and the teaching suits the lantern-name reader. Only small wording clumsiness (ko.otoha_first).

speakerNotes.speaker: ko_otoha
speakerNotes.note: Otoha mixes です/ます with plain musings ('木が、疲れているのです' / '葉が多すぎる'), which is a natural dignified-elder rhythm. The only problem is the meta 'real book' remark in ko.otoha_tellings.

speakerNotes.speaker: cr_jinpachi
speakerNotes.note: おいら plus です/ます, with chatty んで, makes an endearing, consistent character mix that needs learner notes. His FROZEN line names the wrong councillor (ヤエ for タミ).

speakerNotes.speaker: el_genroku
speakerNotes.note: わし/わい/ふん/ぞ without じゃ: strong but consistent old-man role language that suits a gruff, stubborn keeper. It is not stereotyped in this context, but わい needs a note.

speakerNotes.speaker: ko_tokio
speakerNotes.note: Fussy-polite with mutters in plain speech when overworked (ko.tokio_early). The voice is right, but census_ask has a grammatical slip and a counter lesson spoken aloud.

speakerNotes.speaker: nao
speakerNotes.note: Clipped plain throughout, true to profile. Toward the player あんた has become お前 in this late arc (cr.ujie, cr.porch_nao, yn.end), which reads as intended closeness. The one です to Sakichi is a deliberate marker. Watch for maxims delivered as lessons (cr.r2_crew).

speakerNotes.speaker: mio
speakerNotes.note: Soft です/ます to the player, with plain only in emotion, self-talk or to the horse; correctly polite to elders (Kikue, Oshika). Register is consistent. The 薬のラベル analogy recurs four times in this part (a motif rather than a register issue, but heavy).

speakerNotes.speaker: ren
speakerNotes.note: Careful polite with deadpan (getting lost, the kitchen); no oracle-speak. The seven lamp invocations are ritual and fine. Only cr.goto lets a game-mechanic hint into their speech.

speakerNotes.speaker: suzu
speakerNotes.note: Plain with わ/のよ and a stage metaphor in nearly every line, which is consistent but dense. She shifts to です/ます for Ginnojō, correctly. Kansai keeps politeness throughout (片付けますで), but the 〜たねん past forms are non-native and one angry command is softened in dialect.

speakerNotes.speaker: cr_sono
speakerNotes.note: Polite です/ます to the player in all scenes except cr.guestbook, where she becomes chatty feminine plain; that scene is the outlier.

speakerNotes.speaker: cr_heisuke
speakerNotes.note: Firm elder plain with 〜なさい and 御苦労だった, which suits the role; pronoun wobbles once (わし in cr.relay2 against 俺 elsewhere).

speakerNotes.speaker: lf_yae
speakerNotes.note: Courteous polite briefing voice, appropriate. The problem is her name: the nameplate says タミ, but the Cloudroad cast calls her ヤエ.

speakerNotes.speaker: cr_ujie
speakerNotes.note: でございます keigo, consistent and character-defining; keep as is.

speakerNotes.speaker: cr_seibe
speakerNotes.note: Comic でござる used only as a flourish (absent in cr.guest_settle), which works as a joke but needs a learner note.

speakerNotes.speaker: nao
speakerNotes.note: Nao is consistently casual, short and wry. お前 to the player in the Steamhollow quarrel and footbath fits their late-game closeness (earlier regions use あんた). The problems are a few English-shaped phrasings (誰も何も得ない, 俺の足音が自分に, ……正しい。, 愚かな), not register.

speakerNotes.speaker: mio
speakerNotes.note: Mio is polite to every stranger (Oritsu, Rokubei, Tsuneji, Yasuke). She is mostly です/ます to the player in Steamhollow, a guarded arc that is used deliberately, and plain with わ/ね in the Hall and Ashihara. The shift reads as growth, not inconsistency.

speakerNotes.speaker: ren
speakerNotes.note: Ren is careful and polite throughout. Angry lines stay polite, and the deadpan getting-lost puns (帯を三回間違えました。道よりは、少ないです) land. Do not flatten them. Ren is the companion that the all-plain ANY(comp) Hall lines fail.

speakerNotes.speaker: suzu
speakerNotes.note: The standard track is lively and stage-flavoured and fine. The Kansai track in yn has three problems: 私 in five lines where the rest of the game uses うち, 〜たねん instead of 〜てん, and one polite line to Tsuru made plain in Kansai.

speakerNotes.speaker: any
speakerNotes.note: All 51 ANY(comp) lines in this part (mostly Hall puzzle prompts) are plain and have no companion branch. Several end in だ / んだろう / みたいだ, which fits only Nao, and none suits Ren.

speakerNotes.speaker: tsuru
speakerNotes.note: Tsuru is dry plain elder speech (かい, お行き, 〜さ, 〜な) with no 〜じゃ. This is correct and consistent.

speakerNotes.speaker: yn_oritsu / yn_okiyo / yn_tokuzo
speakerNotes.note: There are three distinct inn keigo voices: proud でございます with ますのよ, cheerful くださいまし, and harried humble ございます. They are a good register lesson in themselves. Only くださいまし needs a note.

speakerNotes.speaker: yn_rokubei / yn_tahei
speakerNotes.note: Rokubei's steady plain authority (〜だ, 〜ん, 〜さ) and Tahei's loud ねえ forms are well separated from the Upper House keigo. No change needed.

speakerNotes.speaker: as_mitsue
speakerNotes.note: Mitsue is brisk and warm, and polite throughout. Her one plain わ is in a single parallel branch (fest_prep hill).

speakerNotes.speaker: any (comp)
speakerNotes.note: 45 unique generic lines (105 placements), all plain and casual (ね/だね, plain volitional, a few だ), with no companion branching. They are written in a soft Mio/Suzu-like voice that fits neither Ren (polite throughout) nor Nao (who uses な far more than ね). Several also comment on the grammar rather than the scene.

speakerNotes.speaker: ren
speakerNotes.note: Every Ren-specific line here is です/ます to the player (world intros, reading offers, tale ends); aphoristic but in character. Only the generic comp lines would break this.

speakerNotes.speaker: nao
speakerNotes.note: Casual, short and wry, with natural contractions (立ってる, 思ってた, 慣れてる). The only issue is a repeated 'same as delivery' moral at tale ends.

speakerNotes.speaker: mio
speakerNotes.note: Consistent soft plain with わ/の/ね toward the player. Her tale-end lines alone recite the lesson's grammar list.

speakerNotes.speaker: suzu
speakerNotes.note: Plain with わ/よ plus stage calls (第X幕、幕！). All 20 Kansai versions in this part keep the standard line's casual level; no dialect/politeness conflation was found.

speakerNotes.speaker: hall_shino
speakerNotes.note: Polite (祖父, です/ます) to the party and private おじいちゃん when alone, which is right. One line (shino2 after) mixes the two.

speakerNotes.speaker: hall_mosuke / hall_kihei
speakerNotes.note: Both use folk-tale elder じゃ/〜ん, but it is not a blanket rule for elders (Jinbei plain だ, Kyūbei polite, the priest 〜とも), so it is not a stereotype problem. Learners need a register note.

speakerNotes.speaker: hall_hanbei / hall_ofuku / hall_koun / hall_momo
speakerNotes.note: The four toll-gate travellers are sorted into polite pilgrim, child, plain feminine わ and plain masculine だ. The two adult traders' plain speech to a stranger at a checkpoint is a judgement call for Robin.

speakerNotes.speaker: hall_owan
speakerNotes.note: Simple, childlike plain instructions (〜を取って / 〜方ね), which suit beginner listening material; no issues.

speakerNotes.speaker: hall_ibuki
speakerNotes.note: Clipped plain with 私 throughout fits the anxious, rule-bound young keeper; keep it.

speakerNotes.speaker: nao
speakerNotes.note: Consistently casual and terse, with courier metaphors that work. In the Hall closers (w7–w9) almost every line is an aphorism or a lesson ('一人の話だけを信じると、間違える…'), which is fine one at a time but heavy in sequence. The ending and pages scenes are natural and should stay.

speakerNotes.speaker: mio
speakerNotes.note: Soft plain speech with わ/よ/のね throughout, plus the occasional 〜ましょう invitation, which is natural. Her register to the player in the endings (あなた, ねえ) fits their closeness. The Hall world-closers drift into grammar recaps with a repeated '言葉一つで…のね' formula.

speakerNotes.speaker: ren
speakerNotes.note: Steady です/ます to the player, with plain musing fragments in emotional beats. Both are right. 承知しました comes back four times as a deadpan acknowledgement in pages (keep it, maybe vary it). The real problem is the plain ANY(comp) lines Ren would have to voice.

speakerNotes.speaker: suzu
speakerNotes.note: Plain speech with stage calls (第七幕、幕！) and debt jokes, consistent. The Kansai versions keep the standard line's register and use うち/あんた as docs/dialect/suzu_kansai.md specifies. I found no case where the dialect changes the politeness.

speakerNotes.speaker: any
speakerNotes.note: Every ANY(comp) line in hall w7–w9 has no companion branch and is plain with ね or a volitional ending. They fit Nao, Mio and Suzu, but not Ren. Many are lesson recaps rather than reactions. The 'もう一度言おうか？' template repeats in all ten Hall worlds.

speakerNotes.speaker: hall_otoku
speakerNotes.note: Plain old-wife speech with おくれ/だい to the visitor, and polite (んですか, ましょう, ですね) to her husband and in her 'after' line. That is folk-tale convention, but it runs against the world's own 'plain for family, polite for guests' lesson unless a note covers it.

speakerNotes.speaker: hall tale cast (gonroku, envoy, sabu, saki, gensuke, omatsu)
speakerNotes.note: The role language is deliberate and differentiated: only Gonroku uses じゃ/おる, the envoy has samurai 拙者/参った, Sabu has おいら, while Yosaku and Kichibei, also old men, speak plain. This is not stereotyping, but the marked forms need register notes. Saki's, Gensuke's and Omatsu's polite speech fits their roles.

speakerNotes.speaker: nao
speakerNotes.note: Consistently casual and wry, with short fragments and 俺. The one slip is 私 in atlas.intro.first. 言っておくが to a cat is mock-official, which is fine.

speakerNotes.speaker: mio
speakerNotes.note: Soft plain with わ/のね/かしら to the player across road topics, atlas, guardians and expeditions, and polite to the elder Kikue. That is right. The outlier is the wordplay reflection (and its module), which is fully polite with no bond gate.

speakerNotes.speaker: ren
speakerNotes.note: Careful です/ます with deadpan humour throughout; 参りましょう (x2) is characterful formality, not a fault. Ren never uses だよ/だね, so all nine ANY(comp) lines in this part that use plain ね/よ endings fail for Ren.

speakerNotes.speaker: suzu
speakerNotes.note: Playful plain with stage calls; ハナ without さん is consistent game-wide. The Kansai layer is mostly good (うち/あんた as documented), but 〜たねん is a systematic error (should be 〜てん), and the manzai bit drops stage politeness in Kansai.

speakerNotes.speaker: yasu
speakerNotes.note: Gruff plain わし/〜な/〜ぞ, natural and not caricatured. One stray 俺 in dv.yasu.

speakerNotes.speaker: co_goro
speakerNotes.note: Full old-man role speech (おる/じゃ/〜かの), consistent with his profile and contrasting with Yasu's plainer elder speech. It is fine, but it needs a learner register note.

speakerNotes.speaker: koji
speakerNotes.note: In this part he appears only in the ask-back workshop, speaking announcement keigo that is unlike his casual self elsewhere. It needs framing as an announcement, or a different speaker.
